Study Type: Other: Dermal Developmental Toxicity Study
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Good Lab Practices: Yes
Year Study Performed: 1989
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: ~ 28 days
Species: Rat
Strain: Crl:CD (SD)BR
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 24 pregnant females
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0 (shaved only), 1, 10, 50, 250 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: 1/day for 6 days on gestation days (GD) 0, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18 (unoccluded dermal application to the shaved back)
Exposure period: GD 0-20
Route: Dermal
Results based on critical effect: No deaths occurred throughout the study. The test material did not cause any dermal irritation at any dose. At 250 mg/kg/day, a significant number of females appeared emaciated, with slight dehydration and dark anogenital regions. At 10, 50, and 250 mg/kg/day, a statistically significant increase in the number of females showing a red vaginal exudate (generally associated with resorptions) was noted. Statistically significant decreases in average maternal body weight gain, average body weight and maternal food consumption occurred in all tested groups compared to controls. A significant increase in the number of resorptions at all doses was noted, and the number of dams with all conceptuses resorbed was increased at 10 - 250 mg/kg/day. Average live litter sizes were decreased for all groups and the number of dams administered 10 - 250 mg/kg/day having live fetuses was significantly decreased. Fetal body weights were significantly decreased in groups receiving 1 – 50 mg/kg/day; there were no live fetuses at 250 mg/kg/day. The incidence of pregnancy, or averages for corpora lutea, implantations, or sex ratio per litter for all dose groups were comparable to controls. The test material did not induce fetal malformations at any dose level; however, there were significant increases in the litter or fetal incidences of delayed development of the brain, kidney, thoracic and caudal vertebrae, metacarpals, and hindpaw phalanges. The no observed adverse effect level was reported to be less than 1 mg/kg/day.  
Study Results: NOAEL (maternal and developmental): less than 1 mg/kg/day; LOAEL (maternal and developmental): 1 mg/kg/day.

Study Results: Effects were observed at 1000 ppm and higher.

Other Endpoint Name: Method development 
Test Conditions: Not reported
Submission description: To determine PFOA-generating potential of fluoropolymers when heated just below the melting point, various experiments were performed to determine the optimal methods to extract PFOA. Accelerated solvent extraction (ASE) was used to extract PFOA from polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). Analysis of PFOA concentrations were performed using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). During 3 repeated ASE extractions of PFOA the PTFE material is heated to 150°C for 24 hours prior to the initial methanol extraction. Recovery of PFOA was 1-1.4 ng/g following the first cycle, and recovery was null after the second and third cycles. Varying time intervals were tested up to 120 hours as well as variations in temperature, Relative Humidity, and flow rate. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that PFOA is not readily amenable to transfer in glass vessels due to the adsorption and reaction with glassware and quartz glassware. The form of PFOA does not appear to change this reactivity: salt (Ammonium salt vs. Potassium salt), or free acid form. No differences in recovery were noted between the use of methanol vs. water as a standard, under the conditions established for temperature and airflow, or when standards were prepared and stored in polypropylene.

Study Type: Acute inhalation toxicity with histopathology
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Year Study Performed: 1965
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 14 days; 15- or 30-minute exposure followed by 14-day observation period
Species: Rat
Strain: ChR-CD
Sex of Organisms: Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 4 males
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentration: 2400, 3600, 4800, 6000, 9600 ppm (nominal); 1200, 1800, 2400, 3000, 2400 ppm-hrs (Ct)
Route: Inhalation
Exposure period: 30 minutes at nominal concentrations of 2400, 3600, 4800, and 6000 ppm; 15 minutes at 9600 ppm
Results based on critical effect: Mortality incidences were 0/4, 0/4, 3/4, and 4/4 following a single 30-minute exposure to 2400, 3600, 4800, and 6000 ppm, respectively. Following a single 15-minute exposure to 9600 ppm, 3/4 animals died.  Clinical signs observed in all test substance-exposed groups included lacrimation, salivation, fluid around the nose, intermittent gasping, and inactivity during exposure.  Exposure to lethal concentrations caused cyanosis of the limbs and deep respiration, conjunctival hemorrhage, and/or pigmented secretion around the eyes, and weakness of body and leg muscles.  Temporary corneal opacity was observed in one animal each at 4800 and 9600 ppm.  At sublethal concentrations, respiration was slightly deep during exposure, and thereafter the animals showed weakness in body and leg muscles.  Animals exposed to nonlethal concentrations lost weight for 2 to 3 days, while animals exposed to lethal concentrations showed progressive weight loss until death.  Animals that survived lethal concentrations lost weight for 7 or 14 days post-exposure.  At necropsy, marked reduction in testicular weight and degeneration and necrosis of the germinal cells in the testis were observed at lethal and nonlethal concentrations.  Lung and thymus changes were observed at 14 days in animals exposed to nonlethal concentrations.  The 4-hour approximate lethal concentration is 1200 ppm-hrs.
Study Results: Mortalities at >/= 4800 ppm (15 or 30 min, nominal concentration). Clinical signs at all concentrations, degeneration and necrosis of the testes at lethal and nonlethal concentrations, and lung and thymus changes at nonlethal concentrations. The 4-hour approximate lethal concentration is 1200 ppm-hrs.

Based on these results the submission sponsor finds that the test mixture is a severe eye irritant.
Study Results: Severe corneal opacity (score of 4) and severe conjunctival redness (score of 3) in 6/6 rabbits; severe conjunctival chemosis (score of 4) in 5/6 rabbits; conjunctival petechial hemorrhage, conjunctival blanching, and conjunctival tissue black incolor in 6/6 rabbits. Observed Study Results: The submissions concerns the proceedings of a meeting held on August 20-21, 2004 and DuPont's preliminary analysis of serum lipid data in workers at the Miteni plant in Italy.  The average serum PFOA concentration was approximately 16 ppm with a range of 0.04-92 ppm. Analysis of sera of the PFOA-exposed group also revealed the presence of PFOS (average concentration of approximately 0.5 ppm with a range of 0.06-3.3 ppm). It was concluded from the meeting that serum levels of PFOA were higher in the Miteni workers than have been reported for occupational exposure, and significantly higher than levels reported in the general population.  However, no effects were observed on the general health of the workers at the plant and no changes in clinical chemistry parameters were observed with the exception of slight alteration of serum lipid levels that correlated with exposure.

Observed Study Results: Two data sets were compared to examine the exposure to PFOA for individuals working at a Miteni plant in Italy.  The first data set includes the biological data of all exposed workers since 1987 at 3M and DuPont plants, and the second data set includes the blood analysis of workers at the Miteni site.  The data sets were then merged, and a statistical analysis was conducted.  Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that there was a slight increase of total cholesterol in exposed workers relative to non-exposed workers to PFOA, showing an increasing trend associated with the highest blood PFOA levels; there was no increase of other lipids such as tryglicerides; there was a positive correlation between total cholesterol and PFOA blood levels in the last 4 years, and lastly a slight association between PFOA blood levels and total cholesterol concentrations seems to be consistent over the years.

Results based on critical effect: The test substance induced maternal toxicity at all tested doses.  Effects included mortality (3 and 16 animals at 100 and 150 mg/kg, respectively), inhibition of body weight gain and food consumption (150 mg/kg), and clinical signs of toxicity at all doses (hypoactivity, vocalization, decreased defecation, red material around the eyes and mouth, labored respiration, rales, rapid respiration, gasping, prostration, and lethargy). The NOAEL for maternal and developmental toxicity was <50 mg/kg and 100 mg/kg, respectively.

Clinical signs of toxicity in dams at all doses: hypoactivity, vocalization, decreased defecation, red material around the eyes and mouth, labored respiration, rales, rapid respiration, gasping, prostration, and lethargy. Exophthalmia observed in all treatment groups on GD 6-18.  NOAEL (developmental): 100 mg/kg (based on slightly reduced fetal body weight). Malformations were considered to be spontaneous and fetal development variations were infrequent or at similar frequency as controls.

Stomach polyps in some males and females at 300 ppm and in females at 100 ppm.

Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds dose levels of 500 and 1000 mg/kg/day were severely toxic to rats following 14 days of oral exposure and doses of 100 and 300 mg/kg/day were well-tolerated.
Study Results: Severe clinical findings were noted at 500 and 1000 mg/kg/d and animals were euthanized in extremis. No effects were reported at 100 or 300 mg/kg/d

Study Results: ALD = 2250 mg/kg; mortalities, clinical signs, body weight loss, and gross abnormalities (congestion of the stomach lining).

Good Lab Practices: Yes

Duration of Study: Approximately 10 months
Species: Rat
Strain: Crl:CD(SD)IGS BR(males), Crl:CDBR - VAF/Plus (females)
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 30/sex
Test Substance Purity: 99.5%
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 0.02, 0.06, 0.2, and 0.4% in the diet, corresponding to 0, 16, 48, 160, and 320 mg/kg/day (average, respectively)
Dose Frequency: Daily (diet)
Exposure period: P1 males: 10 weeks prior to mating, through mating until sacrifice; P1 females: 10 weeks prior to mating, during mating, gestation, and postpartum periods, until sacrifice; P2 (F1): PND 21 until sacrifice; F1: PND 21 until vaginal patency (females) or preputial separation (males); F2: PND 21 until vaginal patency (females) or PND 56 (males)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: No treatment-related mortalities or effects on body weight were observed in parental animals.  In P1 animals, increased liver weights (absolute and relative) were observed in both sexes at 0.4%.  Increased kidney weights (absolute and relative) were observed in males at 0.4%.  Additionally, females at 0.4% showed increased relative kidney weights.  In P2 animals, increased liver weights (mean and absolute) were observed in females at 0.2% and 0.4% and in males at 0.4%.  Increased kidney weights (absolute and relative) were observed in males at 0.2% and 0.4%.  Females also showed increased absolute kidney weights at 0.2%.  Kidney effects were considered related to male rat nephropathy and not relevant to humans.  Liver effects were considered related to peroxisome proliferation.
Study Results: Liver and kidney effects were observed at dietary concentrations of 0.2% and higher.

Study Type: Other: Teratologic evaluation 
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Year Study Performed: 1976
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 16 days (exposure on GD 6-15, necropsy on GD 21)
Species: Rat
Strain: Sprague-Dawley
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 29-39
Test Substance Purity: Greater than 99%
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 10, 25, or 65 mg/kg (final); 0, 10, 25, or 65 or 100 mg/kg (preliminary)
Exposure period: GD 6-15
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The test substance produced maternal and developmental toxicity following oral exposure to 25 and 65 mg/kg on GD 6-15.  Developmental effects included increased incidence of fetal malformations (acaudia, short-tail, short trunk, missing vertebrae, and right-sided aortic arch), early resorptions, decreased fetal body weight and crown-rump length, and increased incidence of minor skeletal variants. Maternal toxicity was evidenced by sialodacryoadenitis, hyperexcitability, salivation, thickening of the non-glandular stomach, reduced weight gain, increased water consumption and a single death (at 65 mg/kg). No adverse effects were observed at 10 mg/kg. 
Study Results: Increased incidence of fetal malformations and maternal toxicity at 25 and 65 mg/kg.  Mortality:1/29 at 65 mg/kg (only death).

At the end of the treatment period, Body weight, food consumption, and food conversion efficiency was decreased in 2000 ppm males. Increased glucose was observed in both sexes at 10,000 and 20,000 ppm and males at 4000 ppm males. Increased serum albumin was observed in males at 4000 ppm and greater; albumin/globulin ratios were increased in all treated males. GGT was increased in 20,000 ppm females. increased triglycerides were observed in males (4000 and 10,000 ppm) and females (10,000 and 20,000 ppm). Cholesterol was increased in all treated females and phospholipids were increased in exposed animals of both sexes. Absolute and relative lung weight were increased in both sexes at 10,000 ppm and greater and did not return to control levels following recovery. Absolute and relative spleen weight were decreased in all female groups and males at 10,000 ppm. A dose dependent increase in absolute and relative liver weight was observed in all males and in females at 10,000 and 20,000 ppm. Females of the 20,000 ppm group had a significant decrease in serum creatinine. Increased urinary fluoride was observed in both sexes at 10,000 ppm and greater and in males at 4000 ppm, thereby increasing urinary fluoride/creatinine ratio. Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. Endpoints evaluated include mortality, clinical signs, body weight, food consumption, gross necropsy, organ weight and histopathology. There were five test substance-related deaths in the high dose group (75 mg/kg) as animal were euthanized due to severe weight loss, and clinical signs including piloerection and hunched posture as well as hypothermia and lethargy in some animals. In one animal, the cause of moribundity was stomach ulceration, however no cause or macroscopic evidence of death was found in the other four animals. Clinical signs of salivation were observed in the high dose group. Body weight was reduced in males and in mated females administered 75 mg/kg/d, but not the recovery females (non-mated). Changes in hematology (decreased reticulocytes in both sexes, increased RBC, hemoglobin and hematocrit in males) and clinical biochemistry (increased potassium in males) parameters were noted in rats at the 75 mg/kg/d dose level. At 75 mg/kg/d, increased relative liver weight and hepatocellular hypertrophy, bone marrow atrophy in the sternum and femur, decreased spleen weight and increased extramedullary hematopoiesis were observed in males and all recovered during the recovery period. Thyroid follicular cell hypertrophy was reported in males at 25 mg/kg/d and females at 7.5 mg/kg/d with increased severity with increasing dose. After recovery, males maintained thyroid changes, while females were recovered. Decreased thymus weight at 75 mg/kg/d did not have any associated histological changes. No signs of toxicity were observed in the parental male and female rats treated at 7.5 and 25 mg/kg. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOAEL was 25 mg/kg.
Study Results: Parental NOAEL = 25 mg/kg

The test substance is considered a teratogen in rats; however, a NOAEL for male reproductive effects was not established. Furthermore, the submission sponsor reports that the critical window for these effects is on GD 17-20.
Study Results: Male offspring: reproductive effects observed in all treated groups; NOAEL not established

The test substance was the reaction product of organic acid, halogenated alkane, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide (no CAS # provided). Maternal toxicity occurred at 16000, 24000 and 40000 ppm. Mortality occurred in two females from the 40000 ppm group (GD 16 and 17). Reduced maternal body weight was observed in dams at the highest 3 doses. One severely malformed litter was present in the 24000 ppm dose group. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the dose level of 16000 ppm is both maternally and developmentally toxic.

Results based on critical effect: In a combined repeated dose oral toxicity study with reproduction/developmental toxicity screening test, male and female rats were exposed to the test substance. An additional group of animals were included, but not mated, for a 14-day recovery period in the control and high-dose groups. At 1000 mg/kg bw/day, general signs of reduced health condition were observed in two females prior to being found dead or euthanized after delivery of stillborn pups. This condition was also seen in a third female after delivery of stillborn pups.  Significantly reduced body weight and food consumption were observed in both males and females at 1000 mg/kg bw/day.  Increased absolute and relative liver weights correlating with hepatocellular hypertrophy were observed in both sexes at 1000 mg/kg bw/day, and fatty change was also observed in females. Renal discoloration and tubular cell necrosis was observed in the decedent females, and increased severity of tubular hyaline inclusions in the absence of increased alpha-2-microglobulin content was observed in males. The liver and kidney lesions were not observed after the recovery period. There were no effects at 100 or 300 mg/kg bw/day.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the test substance NOAEL for general systemic toxicity was equal to 300 mg/kg bw/day.
Study Results: systemic toxicity NOAEL = 300 mg/kg bw/day

Observed Study Results: The purpose of the follow-up study was to monitor for the presence of PFOA to evaluate whether there have been changes in PFOA concentrations over time in local waters and biota. Concentrations were compared against the baseline from a 2006 study. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. Results indicate normal operation of the FCC facility results in low, but detectable concentrations of PFOA in stormwater runoff and surficial groundwater immediately beneath the plant. Little impact was recorded in the environment and biota surrounding the plant. Was the study: Measured

Observed Study Results: The Pascagoula Baseline Study was conducted to analyze the PFOA, and provide a “snapshot” of the environment in various media (water, sludge, biota) prior to the startup of a new fluorotelomer operation at the First Chemical site in Pascagoula.  The key findings of the study included the following: all concentrations of PFOA found are consistent with general environmental background levels documented in published scientific studies. All the concentrations of PFOA in water found in this study are well below any current regulatory guidance for drinking water.  Additional findings included the following: PFOA was not detected in Pascagoula drinking water (LOD = 0.0016 ug/L=ppb).  PFOA was not quantifiable in the Pascagoula River, Escatawpa River, Bayou Cassotte, Mississippi Sound or Grand Bay.  PFOA was found at low levels on the First Chemical site and in wastewater discharged from the site of Regional Wastewater Authority, but since PFOA is so widely used, its presence in an area is not necessarily indicative of a local source.  PFOA measured in effluent from the First Chemical site to the Regional Wastewater Authority was a small percentage of the total PFOA measured from the Regional Wastewater Authority outfall to the Pascagoula River.  PFOA was found at low concentrations in some marine life samples.

An increase in specific organ weights (mean absolute thymus gland weights and mean relative liver weights) was also observed.  Effects to the kidneys (minimal to mild pelvic mineralization and secondary transitional epithelium), ovaries (decreased corpora lutea, increased follicular and/or luteinized cysts and interstitial hyperplasia), the mean number of pups born, litter size, pup body weight and body weight gain, mean absolute brain weight of pups, mean and absolute spleen weights, and mean thymus gland weights were also affected.

Results based on critical effect: No mortality was reported. Decreased terminal body weight was reported in 25 and 400 mg/kg-bw/d males. At 400 mg/kg-bw/d, increased absolute and relative liver weight, enlarged liver (4 females) with noted pathology of hypertrophy, nuclear inclusions and necrosis in some animals, as well as, increased bilirubin, triglycerides (males only). No kidney effects were reported, however, decreased creatinine (males only) and increased inorganic phosphates (females only) were observed at 400 mg/kg-bw/d. Increased splenic pigment (iron storage) was observed at greater than 100 mg/kg-bw/d.

Results based on critical effect: The test substance was lethal to 6/15 rats administered 2830 mg/kg via single oral gavage.  Death occurred within 2 days.  Of the 9 survivors, 8 animals were in proestrous for at least 8 consecutive days (starting at 4 days post-dose).  Estradiol levels were decreased within 1 to 2 days post-dose; however, these levels did not appear to follow a normal cyclic pattern until approximately 10 days after dosing. Progesterone levels sharply increased after 1 to 2 days. Body temperature was slightly depressed immediately after dosing but returned to normal within 2 days. Most survivors were in estrus or metestrus and had increased ovary weights. Most animals that died appeared to be in metestrus. The results of this study indicate that the estrous cycle is interrupted following oral exposure at toxic levels to the test substance.

Effects in the dams included salivation and lacrimation (998 ppm) and reduced weight gain (199, 598, and 996 ppm). Effects in the pups included reduced body weights (996 ppm), increased relative kidney and liver weights (598 and 996 ppm), reduced body weight gain (598 and 996 ppm), lowered platelet levels (598 and 996 ppm), low glucose levels (males at all dose levels and females at 996 ppm), elevated GGT levels (both sexes at 996 ppm), and increased relative adrenal weights (males at all dose levels).

Results based on critical effect: The test substance induced clinical signs of toxicity (salivation and lacrimation) in dams at 996 ppm.  There were statistically significant decreases in mean body weights and mean body weight gains at 498 and 996 ppm, and decreases in mean food consumption at 996 ppm.  There were also statistically significant decreases in mean fetal weights.  Fetal examination did not reveal any skeletal malformations; however, visceral malformations and four unrelated malformations were noted (but were not indicated to be treatment-related).  Statistically significant skeletal variations and reduced ossification of the skull and bent ribs were noted at 498 and 996 ppm. Unossification of the hyoid body/arch at 498 and 996 ppm and reduced ossification of the ribs at 996 ppm were also noted, but were not reported to be statistically significant.   These preliminary results require additional analysis before biological significance can be determined.
Study Results: Clinical signs and statistically significant effects (decreases in mean body weights, mean body weight gains, and food consumption; decreases in mean fetal weight; and fetal skeletal variations [reduced ossification of the skull and bent ribs]) were noted in the study.

Reduction in fatty acid synthesis was also observed. The activity of HMG-CoA reductase was reduced by 50% or less, and the activity of acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase (ACAT) was also reduced. The data suggest that the hypolipemic effect of PFOA may be mediated via impaired production of lipoprotein particles due to reduced synthesis and esterification of cholesterol, along with enhanced oxidation of fatty acids in the liver.

Exposure: During his period of employment, the worker had confirmed exposures to acrylonitrile, vinyl chloride, styrene, toluene, ammonia, and mercury. Levels of these chemicals were not available for the main activity of the worker (i.e., as a contact cleaner). Measurements for other areas of the workplace indicated that levels of several of these chemicals were below limit values; however, levels of acrylonitrile, vinyl chloride, and butadiene consistently exceeded limit values.  
Observed Study Results: The worker commissioned an evaluation report by an occupational medical expert to see if his work-related exposure was correlated with his bowel cancer. The expert determined that no correlation could be drawn between the worker's illness and his employment duties; other experts agreed. However, subsequent evaluations, including those of medical experts, of cancer occurrences in co-workers determined that the increase in cancers was probably the result of occupational exposure. Bowel cancer diagnosed in a deceased worker was a result, based on German court proceedings, an occupational illness associated with exposure to one or more of several chemicals, including acrylonitrile.

Results based on critical effect: A cohort mortality study found an elevated standardized mortality ratio (SMR) for lymphosarcoma and reticulosarcoma based on 4 cases (SMR = 5.77, 95% CI: 1.57-14.8). Workers who died of lymphosarcoma and reticulosarcoma (n = 4) had been employed in butadiene units for 9-96 months and death occurred within 25-36 years of initial exposure. Five cases of stomach cancer were noted (SMR = 2.43, 95% CI: 0.79-5.68), all of which occurred following exposure for greater than or equal to 2 years; however, this was not statistically significant.  Based on this data, the submission sponsor finds that the results of the study add to the weight of evidence suggesting that butadiene is carcinogenic to humans.
Study Results: SMR for lymphosarcoma and reticulosarcoma = 5.77, 95% CI: 1.57-14.8; SMR for stomach cancer in all plants = 2.43, 95% CI: 0.79-5.68; SMR for stomach cancer in the Rubber reserve plant = 6.57, 95% CI = 2.13-15.3

Protocol/guideline: Other: OECD 422

Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: At least 5 weeks
Species: Rat
Strain: Crl:CD(SD)
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 10/sex
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Vehicle: Corn oil
Dose/Concentrations: 0,100, 330, and 1000 mg/kg/day (mixture)
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: At least 5 weeks (2 weeks pre-mating, through mating, and post mating until 5 weeks (males); 2 weeks pre-mating, through mating, through gestation, and through post-natal day 13 (females))
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The test substance was administered via gavage to rats at 0,100, 330 or 1000 mg/kg/day.  Endpoints evaluated included clinical signs, body weight, food and water consumption, clinical chemistry, and histopathology (thyroid, liver, kidney, spleen, adrenal glands). Periportal vacuolation was observed in the liver of males at doses greater than or equal to 330 mg/kg/d. In the kidney, cortical tubular pigment was observed in in males at all doses and in females at doses greater than or equal to 330 mg/kg/d. Dose-dependent incidence of hyaline droplets were also observed in males of all doses. Splenic hemosiderosis was observed in both sexes at all doses. In the adrenal gland, cortical vacuolation was observed in all groups (including control) with increased severity at 1000 mg/kg/d males and hypertrophy of the zona glomerulosa was noted in males at doses greater than or equal to 330 and females at the high dose. Follicular cell hyperplasia was observed in both sexes at all doses, correlating with a decrease in serum thyroxine. At all doses in males and an increase in mean plasma TSH at 1000 mg/kg/d in males. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) for systemic toxicity was 330 mg/kg/day. And the LOAEL was 1000 mg/kg/d based on clinical signs, body weight, increased water consumption and changes in thyroid parameters.
Study Results: NOAEL (systemic toxicity) = 330 mg/kg/day LOAEL (systemic toxicity) = 1000 mg/kg/d based on decreased body weight, clinical signs, and changes in thyroid hormones

Results based on critical effect: In a modified extended one-generation reproduction test, male and female parental rats were exposed to the test substance and the litters were used to investigation systemic, neurotoxicological, and immunological endpoints. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following results. At 300 and 1000 ppm, kidney toxicity (degeneration/regeneration of proximal tubules, mineralization at the medulla transition, focal mineralization in the papilla), stomach toxicity (erosion and ulcer, edema in the submucosa with inflammatory cell infiltration), increased urine volume, decreased urine specific gravity, and effects on water and food consumption and body weights were observed in the F0 generation. Similar effects were observed in F1 animals with the addition of centrilobular hypertrophy and fatty change in the liver. At 1000 ppm in F1 animals, decreased number of implants, prolonged/irregular estrous cycles, testicular histopathology (tubular degeneration, immature epithelium, aspermia), ovarian histopathology (luteal cysts, decreased primordial and growing follicles) feminization of male mammary glands, and mammary secretions in females were observed. Decreased pup survival and pub weights were observed at 300 and 1000 ppm.  Neurotoxicity (recurring high-stepping gait, piloerection, impaired auditory startle response, and multifocal degeneration of nerve fibers in the medulla oblongata and spinal cord were observed at 1000 ppm. Increased T4 values were noted in the adults and adolescent males at 1000 ppm, and newborn and weanling females at 100 and 300 ppm. Decreases in the T-helper cells and increases in cytotoxic T-cells in the spleen were also noted.  
Study Results: 300 and 1000 ppm: F0 animals-systemic and  neurological toxicity; F1 animals: systemic, neurological, immunological and reproductive toxicity; 100 ppm: decreased thyroid hormone levels.

The lung and the liver were the primary target organs for treatment-related histopathologic effects following dietary administration for 18 months.  Increases in the incidences and multiplicity (presence of two or more primary tumors in an individual animal) of bronchiolo-alveolar adenomas of the lung were observed in males at 100 and 500 ppm, and in females at 500 ppm. An increased incidence of bronchiolo-alveolar carcinomas was observed in males only at 500 ppm. Treatment-related, non-neoplastic histopathological changes were observed in the lungs of males only at 100 and 500 ppm and included increased incidences of very slight or slight severity multifocal hyperplasia of bronchiolo-alveolar epithelium and very slight, slight, or moderate severity aggregates of alveolar macrophages. Treatment-related liver effects were observed and included increased incidences of hepatocellular adenomas and/or carcinomas in males only 500 ppm. No primary hepatocellular neoplasms were observed in females at any dose level. Increased incidences of very slight or slight severity centrilobular/midzonal hepatocellular hypertrophy, with increased cytoplasmic eosinophilia, were observed at 25 ppm and higher in males and in females at 500 ppm.  Hepatocellular hypertrophy corresponded to increased mean absolute and relative liver weights in males at 500 ppm (13.5% and 9.8% increases, respectively).  Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the test substance induced tumors in the lungs of both sexes and in the liver of males; in addition, hepatocellular hypertrophy in males at 500 ppm was considered adverse because it was accompanied by increased incidences of hepatocellular adenomas and/or carcinomas.
Study Results: Tumors in the lungs (both sexes) and liver (males only); histopathological changes in the liver (hepatocellular hypertrophy) of both sexes (males: all doses; females: 500 ppm).

Exposure period: 90 days

Results based on critical effect: The test substance produced systemic effects in rats following oral exposure to a dose of 450 mg/kg bw/day for 90 days. Effects at this dose included salivation, unspecified changes to urine parameters (protein, ketone, leucocytes) in males, changes to organ weights (kidney and Iiver) in both sexes, and kidney effects (hyaline-like droplets in the epithel cells of proximal convoluted tubules) in males.  The changes in urine parameters (protein levels) were not fully reversible in males. Salivation and slight changes in urine parameters and in liver weights were also observed at 150 mg/kg be/day; however, there was no associated effect on liver function or histopathological changes and weight changes remained within the range of historical controls.  There were no  toxicologically relevant changes in males or females at 40 mg/kg bw/day.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOAEL is 150 mg/kg bw/day.
Study Results: NOAEL: 150 mg/kg bw/day for male and females. Effects: salivation, changes to urinalysis parameters, organ weights, kidney effects at 450 mg/kg.

Number of Organisms per Group: 40 (20/sex)
Test Substance Purity: 97.55%
Vehicle: Corn oil
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 0.5, 2.5, and 10 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 70 days prior to mating, throughout mating, until 1 day prior to euthanasia (males); 14 days prior to mating, throughout mating, gestation, and lactation until 1 day prior to euthanasia (females)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. In a combined repeated dose toxicity study with reproduction/developmental screening, male and female mice were exposed daily to the test substance via oral gavage. No signs of systemic toxicity were noted in females at any dose level during the study or at necropsy. In males, increased body weights and overall body weight gain were noted in the 2.5 and 10 mg/kg/day groups. Macroscopic findings at necropsy consisted of mottled livers and higher mean liver weights in the 2.5 mg/kg/day group and enlarged and mottled livers and higher mean liver weights in the 10 mg/kg/day group. Additionally, adverse microscopic findings of hepatocyte hypertrophy, vacuolation, necrosis, and mixed cellular infiltrates were found in the liver as well as hypertrophy in the adrenal glands at 10 mg/kg/day. Corresponding adverse effects on serum chemistry parameters were also noted at 10 mg/kg/day. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the NOAEL for F0 male systemic toxicity is 0.5 mg/kg/day and the NOAEL for F0 female systemic toxicity is 10 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (males) = 0.5 mg/kg/day; NOAEL (females) = 10 mg/kg/day

Dose Frequency: Daily 
Exposure period: Parental males: 70 days premating, mating, up to 1-day prior to euthanasia; parental females: 14 days premating, mating, gestation, through weaning on postnatal day 22; offspring: postnatal days 22-59
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. In a combined repeated dose study and reproduction/developmental toxicity screening test, male and females mice were exposed to the test substance. Based on the results, the submission sponsor found the following. At 0, 0.5, 2.5, and 10 mg/kg/day, 1/20, 2/20, 3/20, and 3/20 animals were either found dead or euthanized in extremis. Males of the 2.5 and 10 mg/kg day groups exhibited higher mean body weight gains during the entire study period. At 10 mg/kg/day, parental males exhibited the following changes: enlarged and mottled livers, increased terminal body weight, albumin, total protein, globulin, ALP, ALT, AST and SDH concentrations, thyroid weight, adrenal gland weight, and urination count, and decreased T4 level and heart weights. Females of the 2.5 and 10 mg/kg/day groups were recorded having higher thyroid/parathyroid weights. At 0.5, 2.5, 10 mg/kg/day, hypertrophy of hepatocytes and mixed cellular infiltrates with multifocal necrosis of individual hepatocytes were observed in both sexes, and adrenal cortical cell hypertrophy was observed in males at all doses. The NOAEL for systemic toxicity was 0.5 mg/kg/day in males based on changes observed in the adrenal gland and liver. The NOAEL for systemic toxicity in females was 10 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (F0 male systemic toxicity) = 0.5 mg/kg/day; NOAEL (F0 female, F1 offspring systemic toxicity) = 10 mg/kg/day

Results based on critical effect: The study was conducted to examine the latent health effects of PFOA following in utero exposure or an in utero exposure followed by ovariectomy, or exposure as an adult.  Mice were exposed during 17 days of gestation or as young adults.  Gestational exposures occurred in 7-22 dams/group at 0, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, or 5 mg/kg bw/day during GD 1-17.   A subset of developmentally exposed females (n = 8-14/group) exposed to 0, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 1, or 5 mg/kg bw/day during gestation was ovariectomized at 21 or 22 days of age, before the onset of puberty.  A separate cohort of mice (n = 8-14/group) received PFOA starting at 8 weeks of age, for 17 days, at doses of 0, 1, or 5 mg/kg bw/day.  In developmentally exposed mice, there was a reduction in body weight at the highest dose on postnatal day (PND) 1 and at weaning; however, the lowest PFOA doses significantly increased body weight (0.01-0.3 mg/kg bw/day) and increased serum insulin and leptin (0.01-0.1 mg/kg bw/day) during mid-life after developmental exposure.  Ovariectomy caused no additional increase in mid-life body weight.  At 18 months of age, the effects of in utero PFOA exposure on body weight were no longer detected.  Other effects observed in developmentally exposed mice at high PFOA doses included decreased white adipose tissue and spleen weights in intact mice and reduced spleen weight in ovariectomized mice.  Brown adipose tissue weight was significantly increased in both ovariectomized and intact mice at high PFOA doses.  There were no effects of PFOA exposure in mice exposed as adults.  The study demonstrated an important window of exposure for low-dose effects of PFOA on body weight gain, as well as leptin and insulin concentrations during mid-life, in developmentally exposed mice at a lowest observed effect level of 0.01 mg/kg bw/day.  The lowest observed effect level was reported to be 0.01 mg/kg bw/day.
Study Results: Developmental LOAEL = 0.01 mg/kg bw/day, based on reduced body weight at PND 1 and weaning and increased serum insulin and leptin during mid-life.

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. In a prenatal developmental toxicity study, pregnant female rats were administered an experimental pesticide via oral gavage at doses of 0, 100, 300 and 1000 mg/kg bw/d on gestation days 6-19.  Three animals receiving 1000 mg/kg bw/d either died or were sacrificed moribund on study days 7, 8 and 15.  Clinical signs of toxicity in these animals included abdominal position, accelerated respiration, semiclosed eyelids and piloerection. In addition, food consumption was reduced by 66% on study days 6-8 and body weight was reduced by 91% on study day 15. Necropsy of the moribund animal sacrificed on study day 15 showed stomach erosion. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the remaining animals receiving 1000 mg/kg bw/d will be sacrificed early because maternal toxicity exceeded the limit in the test guideline. No abnormal results were reported for the lower doses. The study is ongoing.
Study Results: 1000 mg/kg bw/day = 3/25 died or were sacrificed moribund on study days 7, 8 and 15; body weight loss (91% of control), decreased food consumption (66% of control), stomach erosion (1/25), remaining animals will be sacrificed; 300 and 100 mg/kg bw/day =  no abnormalities.

Dose Frequency: Once
Exposure period: Not reported
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were administered a single dose of the test substance and sacrificed at 96 hours post-dose. Urine and feces were collected throughout the 96-hour post-dosing period. Concentrations of the test substance in the serum and liver were analyzed by LC-MS/MS. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. No mortalities or adverse clinical observations were observed at 96-hours post-exposure. Dose-dependent increases in liver weights (absolute and relative) were observed in both male and female rats; there were no additional significant findings during necropsy. Dose-dependent increases in the serum and non-perfused liver concentrations of the test substance were observed in both sexes at 96 hours post-dosing. Measured concentrations in the serum and liver represented ~25% and 20%, respectively, of the administered dose. LC-MS/MS analyses confirmed that the test substance was being eliminated in both urine and feces.
Study Results: Dose-dependent increases in liver weights; the test substance was found in the serum and liver (25% and 20%, respectively, of the administered dose) and was eliminated in both the urine and feces.

Results based on critical effect: This 91-day dietary study in rats was conducted on the mixture of aspartic acid, ethylene dibromide, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide. Preliminary results have shown degeneration of the seminiferous epithelium in 7/10 and 3/10 males in the 1000 and 700 mg/kg/day groups, respectively. No degeneration was observed at 50 or 300 mg/kg/day. At 1000 mg/kg/day a decrease in normal sperm (85.7% normal compared to 96.7% in controls) and an increase of head only sperm (12.7% compared to 2.3% in controls) was observed but did not occur in the recovery group (with one exception). An increase in abnormal hook sperm was observed at 1000 mg/kg/day (2.4% compared to 1% in controls). Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOEL for the cited observations is well above the maximum anticipated exposures of the test substance, and the submission sponsor estimates a safety factor greater than 400,000-fold for the summarized effects.
Study Results: 700 mg/kg/day: Degeneration of seminiferous epithelium in 3/10 males 1000 mg/kg/day: Degeneration of seminiferous epithelium in 7/10 males. Decrease in normal sperm and an increase in head-only sperm. Increase in abnormal hook sperm.

Results based on critical effect: In a developmental toxicity study, four groups of 25 female Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed via oral gavage to a vehicle control (corn oil) or the test substance at concentrations of 0, 50, 150 and 500 mg/kg/day on gestation days (GDs) 7 through 17. No maternal or fetal mortalities occurred during the study. Maternal clinical signs consisted of excess salivation, urine-stained abdominal fur, red or brown substance on the forepaws, and alopecia in 4-9 rats at 500 mg/kg/day. Reduced maternal body weight gains and food consumption for the entire study period were noted in rats in the 150 and 500 mg/kg/day groups. Pregnancy occurred in 25, 24, 24, and 21 females in the 0 (control), 50, 150, and 500 mg/kg/day dose groups, respectively. Fetal weights were reduced in the 500 mg/kg/day group. No differences in litter averages for corpora lutea, implantations, litter size, live/dead fetuses, early/late resorptions, percent resorbed conceptuses, or percent male fetuses were noted in any dose group. Malformations occurred in 1, 0, 2, and 6 fetuses from 1, 0, 2, and 5 litters in the four respective dosage groups. Only malformations in the 500 mg/kg/day group, which included skeletal variations, were considered to be related to the test substance. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the maternal NOAEL for the test substance is 50 mg/kg/day and the developmental NOAEL is 150 mg/kg/day.

Strain: Crl: WI(Han)

Number of Organisms per Group: 20 (10/sex)
Test Substance Purity: > 99%
Vehicle: Corn oil
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 100, 300, and 1000 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Daily
Exposure period: 29 days (males), 50-62 days (females)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Endpoints evaluated include mortality, clinical signs, body weight, food consumption, functional observations, gross necropsy, organ weights and histopathology. Slightly decreased body weight gains and food consumption noted in males at 1000 mg/kg/day were considered non-adverse.  Clinical chemistry alterations that were considered non-adverse included elevated alanine and aspartate aminotransferase activity (males at 300 and 1000 mg/kg-bw/day), decreased potassium (males at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day), decreased mean total bilirubin (females at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day), and increased cholesterol (females at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day.  At 1000 mg/kg/day increased kidney weight was reported in males with elevated serum urea and creatinine observed in both sexes. Kidney lesions and histopathological findings included urothelial hypertrophy of the bladder (both sexes), and increased incidence and/or severity of tubular basophilia and dilation of the kidneys in both sexes and renal tubular casts in males. Urinary bladder exhibited histological signs of urothelial hypertrophy in both sexes at 300 and 1000mg/kg/day.  Tubular dilation and tubular basophilia were noted in females at 100 and 300 mg/kg-bw/day but were not considered adverse. Squamous cell hyperplasia was observed in the stomach (both sexes at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day) and lymphoid depletion was observed in the thymus (both sexes at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day and females at 300 mg/kg-bw/day).  A treatment-related reduction in serum T4 levels was noted in F0 males. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the NOAEL for parental toxicity is 100 mg/kg-bw/day, based on histopathological findings in the bladder of males at 300 mg/kg-bw/day. 
Study Results: NOAEL (parental) = 100 mg/kg/day; LOAEL (parental) = 300 mg/kg/day

Results based on critical effect: In a definitive developmental toxicity test in rats, maternal toxicity was evident at 1500 and 3500 ppm.  Effects at 3500 ppm included mortality, reduced body weight, increased liver weight, and treatment-related clinical signs of central nervous system depression (ataxia, gasping, rough coat, lethargy, squinted eyes, head tremors and slow respiration. At 1500 ppm, liver weights were increased and there were limited clinical signs of CNS depression (half closed eyes and head tremors). Developmental toxicity was evidenced by an increase in the incidence of late fetal deaths, reduced fetal body weight per litter and an increased incidence of cleft palate (11 fetuses in 6 litters) at a dose of 3500 ppm. Study authors believe that maternal stress was the cause of cleft palate in developing fetuses. The maternal no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) was reported to be 250 ppm, and the developmental NOAEL was reported to be 1500 ppm.  
Study Results: No evidence of cleft palate was found; NOAEL (maternal): 250 ppm; NOAEL (developmental): 1500 ppm. Maternal toxicity at 3500 ppm: mortality, reduced body weight, increased liver weight, treatment-related clinical signs of central nervous system depression. At 1500 ppm, increased liver weight and limited clinical signs of CNS depression.

Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The study was to determine the doses for the planned OECD 422 study. The substance was toxic at 450 mg/kg bw/day and was reduced to 300 mg/kg bw/day on day 7. One male and one female were euthanized due to toxicity at 450 mg/kg bw/day. Paternal effects included decreased absolute and relative prostate weight, increased absolute and relative liver and spleen weights, and altered red blood cell counts.  Maternal effects (clinical signs, effects on blood, spleen, liver) and changes to the reproductive parameters (number of corpora lutea, pre- and post-implantation loss, litter weight) were observed in the high dose group.  One female in the high dose group did not deliver live pups and another female had 100% pup mortality by PND 1. The study authors concluded that the prenatal litter loss and postnatal survival may have been impacted by maternal toxicity.  In the mid-dose there were changes to blood parameters and absolute and relative organ weight changes.  In the low dose, there were changes to the blood parameters.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the substance induces effects in rats. A NOAEL was not given.    
Study Results: Range finding study.  Paternal effects at 150 and/or 300/450 mg/kg bw/day: decreased prostate weight, increase in spleen and liver weights, altered hematology; maternal effects at 150 and/or 300-450 mg/kg bw/day: clinical signs, altered hematology parameters, increase in spleen and liver weights, altered number of corpora lutea, pre- and post-implantation loss, and litter weight.

Results based on critical effect: The test substance produced maternal toxicity in rats following dietary exposure on gestation days 6-21.  Effects included decreased body weight (up to 34.8% with final bw decreased by 14.0%) correlated with decreased food consumption at 7000 ppm; hematological effects (decreased RBC count, hemoglobin concentration, hematocrit, and mean  MCHC and increases in MCV, MCH, platelet count and reticulocyte count) at all doses; and increased absolute and relative spleen weights at 7000 ppm. No clinical signs of toxicity were evident. There were no treatment-related effects on pregnancy rate, number of corpora lutea, implantations, resorptions, pre- or post-implantation loss, or litter size  at any dose level tested. A single litter at 7000 ppm had multiple external craniofacial malformations, which were considered by study authors to be spurious and unrelated to treatment.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the test substance was maternally toxic, but did not produce developmental toxicity.
Study Results: Maternal toxicity at all dose levels. Decreased body weight (up to 34.8%) correlated with decreased feed consumption at 7000 ppm; hematological effects at all doses; increased spleen weights at 5000 and 7000 ppm.  No treatment-related effects on pregnancy rate, number of corpora lutea, implantations, resorptions, pre- or post-implantation loss, or litter size  at any dose level tested. Single litter at 7000 ppm with multiple external craniofacial malformations; considered to be unrelated to treatment.

In a 2 week range-finding study, the test substance was administered to male and female rats in the diet. Endpoints evaluated included mortality, clinical signs, body weight changes, food and water consumption, gross pathology, and organ weight. At 5000 ppm, 1 female and 2 males were found dead, one female was sacrificed moribund, and the remaining animals were sacrificed premature. Clinical signs at this dose level consisted of semi-closed eyelids (4 males and 3 females), general poor condition (3 males and 1 female), piloerection, hunched posture, and hard abdomen (1 male and 1 female), and hypothermia (1 female). Decreased food consumption and body weight loss were also observed in all animals. At 2500 ppm, 1 male and 1 female were sacrificed moribund after 3 days of administration. Additionally, decreased food consumption and mean body weight loss within the first 3 days of administration were observed in all animals, and semi-closed eyelids were observed in 4 males and 6 females. No effects were observed at 850 ppm. This study is ongoing.
Study Results: 5000 ppm: mortality in all animals, found dead or sacrificed in extremis, severe clinical signs and body weight reduction; 2500 ppm: 1 male and 1 female sacrificed moribund on day three

Results based on critical effect: In response to a class action lawsuit, members of the C8 Panel analyzed evidence to see if there was an association between PFOA exposure and pregnancy induced hypertension.  Four studies were evaluated.  The first study examined the relationship between water service area and pregnancy-induced hypertension, the second examined the relationship between PFOA levels in the serum, the third was a companion to the second study and linked the birth records to pregnancies of the women in the study, and the fourth examined the relationship between serum and pregnancy induced hypertension when PFOA was removed from municipal water supplies.  It was concluded that there is evidence for an association between PFOA and pregnancy induced hypertension and that there is a probable link to the disease among class members.  
Study Results: There was evidence of an association between PFOA exposure and pregnancy induced hypertension; it was concluded that PFOA has a probable link to this disease among class members.

Results based on critical effect: A "probable link" between PFOA exposure and pregnancy induced hypertension and preeclamsia was investigated in 4 epidemiology studies.  Study 1 investigated the relationship between water service area and pregnancy-induced hypertension. Studies 2 and 3 utilized birth records; Study 4 addressed pregnancy-induced hypertension in Class Members after enrollment in the C8 Health Project. There was no association between pregnancy-induced hypertension and zip codes and there was little support for an association based on the full residential history. There was evidence of an association between estimated serum PFOA and pregnancy-induced hypertension (n=106) based on the continuous exposure indicator (adjusted odds ratio = 1.25 comparing the 75th to the 25th percentiles of exposure). Measured serum PFOA was weakly and irregularly associated with preeclampsia (n=156) and there was an elevated risk for women above the 50th percentile of exposure (odds ratio = 1.3).  Results of self-reported preclampsia (n=730) showed a modest association with estimated serum PFOA at the time of pregnancy (odds ratio for continuous exposure indicator = 1.13, comparing the 75th and 25th percentiles of exposure). The association between estimated serum PFOA and preeclampsia was strengthened when the analysis was restricted to more recent pregnancies (2000-2005), with adjusted odds ratios in the upper quintiles ranging from 1.3-1.5. At 500 mg/kg-bw/day, one male was found dead and one was sacrificed in moribund state. Clinical signs consisted of piloerection and salivation in both sexes and labored respiration, gasping, and respiration sounds in males only. Food consumption was significantly decreased in males from study days 0-3 and in females from study days 3-7. Body weight was decreased in males from study days 0-3 and reduced body weight gain occurred in both sexes. At necropsy, increased relative liver weights were noted in females and pathological findings of the GI tract included forestomach and glandular stomach foci, thickened stomach wall and duodenum, dilated jejunum, discolored jejunum content, discoloration of mesenteric lymph node. No relevant findings were reported at 150 mg/kg bw/day. This study is ongoing.
Study Results: 500 mg/kg-bw/day: Mortality in 2 males, clinical signs of toxicity, decreased food consumption and reduction in body weight gain, increased relative liver weight (females), GI pathology; 150 mg/kg-bw/day: No effects noted

Observed Study Results: A study on the occurrence of HBCD, TBBP-A and Me-TBBP-A in sewage sludge, sediments and biota of The Netherlands, UK and Ireland was carried out in order to trace possible sources, understand behaviors and to study distribution in the aquatic environment. TBBP-A and MeTBBP-A were absent in all landfill samples from the UK and Ireland. However, in Dutch landfill samples these compounds were found. TBBP-A was almost in all cases found in much lower concentrations than HBCD, as well as in biota as in sediments. In some cases it was found in the dissolved phase of the influent of some UK STPs. The lower TBBP-A concentrations in sediments may be explained by the way TBBP-A is used as a flame retardant, i.e. as a reactive compound. TBBP-A will therefore be stronger bound and less easily leave the matrix in which it has been used. The more polar character of TBBP-A limitsits bioaccumulation potential. Also, easier excretion mechanisms in biota and possible degradation mechanisms may explain the lower TBBP-A concentrations in biota, since the phenolic group of TBBP-A allows conjugation to endogenous compounds (e.g. glucoronic acid and sulfate) without the necessity of any phase-I biotransfomation prior to it. The MeTBBP-A concentrations were generally low, but its bioaccumulation potential is higher than that of TBBP-A.

Maternal toxicity included reduced body weight gain, uterine weight and liver weight (10 mg/kg bw/day), reduced food consumption (3 and 10 mg/kg bw/day), reductions in red cell distribution width (%), cholesterol, chloride, and triglycerides and increased red blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit (absolute), albumin, total protein, globulin, glucose, calcium, and phopshorus at 10 mg/kg bw/day, and cholesterol was reduced at 3 mg/kg bw/day. Post-implantation loss, attributed to early resorptions (46.3%) and reduced fetal weight were observed at 10 mg/kg bw/day.  External malformations occurred in 24 fetuses in 7 separate litters at 10 mg/kg bw/day and included omphalocele, gastroschisis, thoracogastroschisis, cheilognathoschisis, cleft lip, exencephaly with open eyelid, anasarca, localized fetal edema, ectrodactyly, paw hyperextension, paw malrotated, bent tail, short tail, and/or micromelia.
Study Results: Maternal toxicity: reduced body weight gain, uterine weight and liver weight (10 mg/kg bw/day); reduced food consumption (3 and 10 mg/kg bw/day); significant changes in hematology and clinical chemistry (3 and 10 mg/kg bw/day).  Developmental toxicity: post-implantation loss attributed to early resorptions and reduced fetal body weight and external malformations (10 mg/kg bw/day).

Study Type: Other: Epidemiology

Results based on critical effect: The submission sponsor used data from the University of Alabama Birmingham epidemiological study on worker exposure to butadiene in the styrene-butadiene rubber industry to develop Poisson linear rate ratio models and Cox proportional hazards log linear ratio models to estimate added risk for leukemia. Both final models adjusted for age and cumulative DMDTC exposure. Risks were calculated at 85 years of age with 45 years of occupational exposure to butadiene and based on European survival and mortality rates. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that based on the Cox proportional hazards log linear ratio model, the maximum likelihood estimate and 95% upper confidence interval for added risk per million based on exposure to 0.1 ppm are: 0 and 4.14 for acute myelogenous leukemia; 1.61 and 2.45 for chronic lymphocytic leukemia; and 0.07 and 1.88 for chronic myelogenous leukemia. Furthermore, the slope of the cumulative butadiene ppm-years in the rate ratio was only statistically significantly different from the null for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (Cox proportional hazards modeling only).
Study Results: MLE for added risk per million: 0 (95% upper CI = 4.14) for acute myelogenous leukemia; 1.61 (95% upper CI = 2.45) for chronic lymphocytic leukemia; and 0.07 (95% upper CI = 1.88) for chronic myelogenous leukemia

Protocol/guideline: Other: OECD 429
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 4 days
Species: Mouse
Strain: CBA/J
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 5 females/group
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Vehicle: DMF
Doses: 1%, 2.5%, 5% w/w
Dose Frequency: Once daily
Exposure period: Approximately 6 days
Route: Dermal
Results based on critical effect: Groups of mice received daily applications of the test substance (25 uL) to the dorsum of both ears at a concentration of 1%, 2.5%, or 5% w/w in DMF for 3 consecutive days. A group of control animals similarly received applications of the vehicle only. Three days following the last application, the mice received an intravenous injection of 20 uCi of 3H-thymidine in sterile saline into a tail vein. Approximately 5 hours after the injection, the animals were euthanized and the auricular lymph nodes were collected. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. No signs of systemic toxicity were observed. The test substance induced a statistically significant increase in 3H-thymidine incorporation into the cells of the auricular lymph nodes, which exceeded the cutoff value for biological relevance (stimulation index of 3) at all concentrations tested (1%, 2.5%, and 5%); therefore, it was concluded that the test substance exhibited a skin sensitizing potential in the LLNA. At all concentrations, the test substance also induced statistically significant increases in the following indices: cell count, lymph node weight, and ear weight.
Study Results: Positive for skin sensitization.

Was the Study: Measured

Species: Rabbit

Sex of Organisms: Female

Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 500 and 750 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Not reported
Exposure period: 23 days

Results based on critical effect: Pregnant rabbits were exposed from day 6 through day 28, post insemination. Maternal toxicity was severe and included: drastically reduced food consumption, body weight, body weight gain, and defecation at 750 mg/kg/day. The treatment concentration was reduced to 500 mg/kg/day, but clinical signs did not improve and 6 of the 25 does aborted. All animals with adverse clinical signs were sacrificed, and the remaining 3 were sacrificed before the end of the test due to abortions. Macroscopic findings included stomachs full of dry, hard feed in 16/25 animals and stomach ulcerations in 7/25 animals. No effects were reported on offspring due to the severe maternal toxicity and abortions.
Study Results: Severe maternal clinical signs (reduced food consumption, body weight, body weight gain, and defecation) required a dose reduction from 750 mg/kg/day to 500 mg/kg/day; 6/25 animals aborted after this reduction. No animals survived until study completion due to severe clinical signs and abortions. No effects of offspring were reported due to abortions.

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission.  No mortalities occurred.  Animals were exposed for 1 hour to mean concentrations of 10,300, 26,000, and 47,700 ppm.  An additional group of four male rats were exposed for 4 hours to a mean test concentration of 10,200 ppm.  Rats exposed to dose concentrations less than or equal to 26,000 ppm (for either 1 or 4 hours) displayed no clinical signs of toxicity throughout the entire study and displayed normal startle responses during the exposures. Male and female rats in the 47,000 ppm group displayed impaired balance, staggered gait, decreased startle response and decreased activity after approximately 15 minutes of exposure. After approximately 55 minutes of exposure, all rats displayed immobility and no startle response. ln addition, one male rat was prostrate for the last 5 minutes of the exposure.  These rats displayed normal alerting response within 7 minutes of when the liquid test substance flow was shut off. However, all rats were lethargic and the male rat that was prostrate during the final 5 minutes of the exposure also displayed slow and labored breathing after the exposure, as well as the next day. There were no other clinical signs of toxicity observed in rats from the 47,700 ppm group throughout the remainder of the recovery period.  Body weight gains were observed in rats at 10,300 ppm, and losses were recorded for animals at 26,000 and 47,700 ppm.  Rats in the additional dose group (10,200 ppm) lost weight on day 1 of exposure followed by normal weight gain throughout the study.  Based upon these results, the study sponsor finds the 1-hour and 4-hour ALC values to be greater than 47,700 ppm and greater than 10,200 ppm, respectively.
Study Results: 1-hour ALC is greater than 47,700 ppm in rats; 4-hour ALC is greater than 10,200 ppm in male rats.

The test substance was administered to Wistar Rats at 0.3, 0.908, and 1.881 mg/L (analytical concentration). During the post exposure examination, changes to the alveoli and lungs were observed in one female at the mid concentration. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the lethal concentration that killed 50 percent of the population was 0.883 mg/L in males and greater than 1.881 mg/L in females.

Medium: Other: Environmental Monitoring-Soil Media
Protocol/Guideline: Not reported
Location: Wallingford, CT
Was the study: Measured
Exposure period: Not reported
Observed Study Results: Cytec Industries Inc., is reporting the preliminary results of analyses recently conducted at its Wallingford, CT facility.  The results of the analyses indicate the presence of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in the soil at this site in a localized area covered with asphalt.  The results of one of the seven soil borings indicate a concentration of 7200 ppm at a depth of nine feet below grade.  The other soil borings show lower levels of PCBs.  At this time, Cytec believes that the soil contamination has resulted in little, if any, exposure over the years.  The ground above the localized area is not only covered with asphalt but is also surrounded by a loading dock foundation and a railroad spur.  Studies have been completed to determine the boundaries of the soil contamination in three of the four directions.  The study to define the fourth boundary is still underway.  Also, there are two groundwater monitoring wells in close proximity to the contamination.  These wells are currently being sampled to assure that there is no groundwater contamination.  Cytec is also reporting these findings to the CT DEP and USEPA Region I as a historical release.  This conclusion is based on the fact that the heat transfer fluid in the process building was Arochlor 1248, a PCB containing material.  This material was used in the 1950s and replaced in the early 1960s with a non-PCB containing heat transfer fluid.  This was the only time that PCB containing materials were used in the building immediately adjacent to the area of contamination.

Slight reductions in body weight and body weight gain (associated with reduced food consumption) was observed in both sexes throughout the dosing period. The submission sponsor did not include information about results from the reproductive, neurotoxicity, neuropathology, or immunotoxicity examinations. No effects on hematology or clinical chemistry was observed in parental animals of the main study. Females of the 2800 ppm satellite group had smooth ovoid crystals (10-40 microns) of various shapes in urinalaysis examinations. P1 females had treatment related renal tubular degeneration at doses greater than or equal to 1000 ppm. Additional kidney effects were observed in P1 males dosed at 1000 ppm and greater and P1 females dosed at 2800 ppm; these effects included slight hypertrophy of centrilobular/midzonal hepatocytes with increased cytoplasmic eosinophilia. P1 males and females dosed at 2800 ppm had urinary bladder effects including very slight or slight simple diffuse urothelial hyperplasia and a very slight multifocal subacute to chronic inflammation in the lamina propria. 
Study Results: 1000 ppm: kidney effects (males and females); 2800 ppm: kidney effects (males and females), urinary bladder effects (males and females), ovoid crystals in urinalysis (satellite females only)

Was the Study: Measured

Exposure period: 2 weeks before mating, during mating and, for the males, until sacrifice, for the females, throughout gestation until Day 4 postpartum
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. The test substance was lethal to 2/10 males and 8/10 females from the 100/80 mg/kg/day group.  Clinical signs of toxicity in rats that died or were sacrificed moribund included piloerection, round back, hypoactivity, abdominal breathing, dyspnea, ptyalism, half closed eyes and/or chromorhinorrhea, chromodacryorrhea, locomotory difficulty, and animals which were cold to the touch. Round back was also observed in animals from the 50 mg/kg group.  When compared with controls, there was a lower fertility index at 100/80 mg/kg/day.   At 50 mg/kg/day and when compared with controls, there was a low mean number of pups delivered at birth (10.0 vs. 14.0).  The reduced fertility index and the reduced number of viable pups at birth were both lower than the limit of historical control data. A marked increase in pups which were found dead, moribund, or cannibalized as well as pups that were cold to the touch were noted at 100/80 mg/kg/day.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOAEL for parental and reproductive toxicity is 25 mg/kg/day, and the NOAEL fetal toxicity is 50 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (parental toxicity) is 25 mg/kg/day (based on clinical signs from 50 mg/kg/day and, mortality in both sexes at 100/80 mg/kg/day). NOAEL (reproduction) is 25 mg/kg/day (based on the lower number of pups delivered from 50 mg/kg/day). NOAEL (fetal toxicity) is 50 mg/kg/day (based on the low pup viability at 100/80 mg/kg/day)

Results based on critical effect: The mixture, known as "Epi-Cure 8701", was instilled into the conjunctival sac of the right eye of 6 rabbits.  At 1-hours post-instillation through 72 hours, chemical burns, epithelial sloughing and/or free blood were observed.  By 7 days post-instillation corrosion and loss of lens were observed in all animals.  The level of necrosis and corrosion was so extensive that the study was terminated on day 7.  The average irritation scores at 1, 24, 48, and 72 hours and 7 days post-instillation were 64.7, 65, 75.8, 79.8, and 110.0, respectively. Based on these results the submission sponsor finds that the test substance is a severe eye irritant.

Study Type: Other
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported

Was the Study: Measured

Dose/Concentration: 266.7, 400, 600, 900, 1350, 2025 and 3038 mg/kg (undiluted dose of mixture)
Route: Dermal
Exposure period: 24 hours
Results based on critical effect: The mixture, known as "Epi-Cure 8701", was administrated undiluted to the clipped intact or abraded skin of young albino rabbits for 24 hours. The mortality incidence was 0/4, 2/4, 1/4, 0/4, 3/4, 4/4 and 4/4 at 266.7, 400, 600, 900, 1350, 2025 and 3038 mg/kg, respectively. Hypoactivity and muscular weakness was observed in all rabbits at 900, 1350, 2025 and 3038 mg/kg 6-22 hours after exposure.  At 900 mg/kg, the rabbits recovered from the hypoactivity and muscular weakness.  In addition, diarrhea was also noted in all rabbits at 900 mg/kg on day 4 of observation with no recovery. Body weight was reduced in most surviving animals through the test period.  Extreme skin irritation characterized by third degree burns and severe edema was observed on test sites after 24 hours and necrosis was present in survivors at 7 and 14 days. Necropsy revealed emaciation and depletion of body fat stores, enlarged gall bladders, pale kidneys, hemorrhaged lungs, and moderate to advanced postmortem autolysis. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the LD50 is 872.97 mg/kg.
Study Results: Mortality incidence: 0/4, 2/4, 1/4, 0/4, 3/4, 4/4 and 4/4 at 266.7, 400, 600, 900, 1350, 2025 and 3038 mg/kg, respectively. Hypoactivity and muscular weakness in all rabbits at 900, 1350, 2025 and 3038 mg/kg 6-22 hours after exposure.  Diarrhea in all rabbits at 900 mg/kg on day 4 of observation with no recovery. Body weight loss in most surviving animals through the test period.  Extreme irritation characterized by third degree burns and severe edema and necrosis. Necropsy revealed emaciation and depletion of body fat stores, enlarged gall bladders, pale kidneys, hemorrhaged lungs, and moderate to advanced postmortem autolysis. LD50 = 872.97 mg/kg.

Study Type: Other: Reproductive/developmental toxicity screening
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: At least 90 days
Species: Rat
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: Not reported
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 1, 20, and 80 (reduced to 50 on Day 44) mg/kg-bw/day
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 10-week premating, 1-week mating, through gestation and lactation until 14 days after delivery (at least 90 days)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Four treatment-related deaths (three males, one female) occurred in the high dose group during treatment. No mortalities occurred in any of the other groups. Signs of toxicity in the high dose group included nasal and retinal discharge, crustiness around the eyes, ears, nose, and legs, dirtied fur/fur standing up, lethargy, irregular posture, macrophthalmia, weak muscles, dyspnea, thinness, and swollen limbs. Also observed in the high dose level was the decline in mean body weights and consumption of feed in all sexes. Clinical biochemistry findings in this group included decreased cholesterol and phospholipid levels in males. Gross macroscopic findings included relatively elevated liver and kidney weights in males, large spleens, mesenteric lymph nodes, and small pale spots on the lungs and the liver. Treatment-related effects at the mid-dose level included decreased cholesterol and phospholipid levels (males), increased urea and potassium levels (males), liver effects in males (minimal to moderate centrilobular hepatocellular microvacuolation), alveolar macrophages in lungs (both sexes). No effects were observed on estrous cycle, fertility, reproductive performance, or T4 hormone. No effects were observed on offspring. Based on the results, the submission sponsor find that the test substance yields a parental NOAEL of 1 mg/kg-bw/day, and a fertility and developmental NOAEL of greater than or equal to 20 mg/kg-bw/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (parental) = 1 mg/kg-bw/day; NOAEL (fertility and developmental) >/= 20 mg/kg-bw/day

Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 28 days
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: No mortalities occurred during the study. Clinical observations including hunched posture and tiptoe gait were observed in high dose females. Reduced body weight was observed in high dose animals and mid dose males. Reduced food consumption and food conversion efficiency were observed in high dose animals. Increased water consumption was observed in high dose animals and mid dose males. Hematology revealed increase in platelet count in high dose animals; reductions in hemoglobin, total erythrocyte, and hematocrit levels in high dose males; and reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin and mean corpuscular volume in high dose females. Increased calcium concentration were observed in high dose males. Increased absolute and relative liver weight was observed in dose groups greater than or equal to 100 mg/kg bw/day and at 300 mg/kg bw/day, enlarged, dark livers were noted in necropsy with histological evidence of diffuse hypertrophy, pale, eosinophilic cytoplasm, increased mitotic cells in males and centrilobular hypertrophy and one incidence of diffuse change and one incidence of increased mitotic cells in females. Increased cholesterol was also reported in high dose animals. Minimal centrilobular hepatocyte hypertrophy was reported in both sexes at 100 mg/kg bw/day and males only at 30 mg/kg bw/day. At the high dose, males had reduced size and reduced absolute and relative prostate and seminal vesicle weight as well as degeneration of the tubules (testes) and increased cellular debris in the epididymis. There was also atrophy of the accessory glands with accompanied decrease in secretions. At 100 mg/kg bw/day only one male exhibited similar effects. At doses greater than or equal to 100 mg/kg bw/day there was evidence of hypertrophy in the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal gland. Based on the results, the submission sponsor concludes that the NOAEL is 30 mg/kg-bw/day for males (the submission sponsor considered liver changes at 30 mg/kg bw/day to be adaptive).
Study Results: NOAEL = 30 mg/kg-bw/day; LOAEL = 100 mg/kg bw/day based on liver weight and histology and male reproductive organ weight and histology.

Observed Study Results: The submission concerns ambient exposure to a mixture of sodium hyperchlorite and ammonia that resulted in the formation of chloramine gas. On September 25, 2000, an accidental death was reported from the misuse of Clorox brand Professional Strength Liquid Plumr product.  The victim, a 74 or 77 year old female was found dead in her bathtub; the actual time of death is estimated as sometime on Saturday, September 23. She was not bathing. Quart bottles of Professional Strength Plumr and Parsons lemon scented ammonia were in the bathtub.  The preliminary cause of death from the autopsy is "complications of chemical inhalation and contact" and "drowning".  The coroner's hypothesis is that the woman accidentally mixed the cleaning products, was overcome by fumes, collapsed into the bathtub and drowned.  The autopsy revealed pulmonary edema and chemical burns to the skin around the ankles and genitalia.  Clorox contends that the case of death is unusual.

Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: Not reported

Vehicle: Not reported

Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)

Results based on critical effect: In females of the 1000 mg/kg treatment group, increased incidence of follicular cell hypertrophy (minimal or slight) in the thyroid and a decrease of T4 (on average 19%) were recorded. Pups of the 1000 mg/kg treatment group had lower live birth index (91% vs 100%),statistically significant decreased mean pup weights at PND 1, and lower mean pup weights at PND 4 and 7. Pups of the 1000 mg/kg group were found dead at first litter check (9 pups from 3 litters) and at PND 1 and 4 (4 pups from 3 litters). 
Study Results: Female 1000 mg/kg treatment group showed increased incidence of follicular cell hypertrophy (minimal or slight) in the thyroid and a decrease of T4 (on average 19%); pups of the 1000 mg/kg treatment group showed lower live birth index (91% vs 100%), statistically significantly decreased mean pup weights at PND 1, lower mean pup weights at PND 4 and 7.  Mortality was noted in pups at 1000 mg/kg (9 pups from 3 litters at the first litter check, 4 pups from 3 litters between PND 1 and 4).
