Results based on critical effect: The test substance was lethal to 2/10, 4/10, 8/10, 7/10, and 10/10 male and 2/10, 9/10, 10/10, 10/10, and 10/10 female rats at 15, 25, 35, 50, and 75 mg/kg-bw, respectively. Clinical signs of toxicity in surviving animals and animals that died included depression, trembling, lacrimation, wet belly, salivation, prostration, and occasional ataxia. All survivors were normal in appearance after day 7 post-administration. Necropsy in animals that died revealed darkened appearance of the livers and kidneys, hemorrhagic lungs, and sloughing and/or inflammation and erosion of the stomach mucosa. There were no significant necropsy findings in surviving animals. The LD50s for males and females were 27 and 18 mg/kg, respectively.
Study Results: LD50 (males); 27 mg/kg; LD50 (females): 18 mg/kg. Mortality incidence: 20, 40, 80, 70, and 100% of males and 20, 90, 100, 100, and 100% of females at 15, 25, 35, 50, and 75 mg/kg-bw, respectively. Clinical signs in all animals: depression, trembling, lacrimation, wet belly, salivation, prostration, and occasional ataxia. All survivors normal by 7 days post administration. Necropsy in animals that died: dark appearance of livers and kidneys, hemorrhagic lungs, sloughing and/or inflammation and erosion of the stomach mucosa. No significant necropsy findings in survivors.

Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 12/sex
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 15, 30, 60/90 mg/kg bw/day
Dose Frequency: Daily 
Exposure period: Male: 6 weeks; female: 2 weeks premating, mating, gestation through lactation day 13
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: In a reproduction/developmental toxicity screening test, male and female Wistar rats were exposed to the test substance. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds the following. At 90 mg/kg bw/day, two females and one litter were terminated prematurely, resulting in the reduction of the dose to 60 mg/kg bw/day. Two males at 30 mg/kg bw/day and one male at 60/90 mg/kg bw/day showed flaccid testes and small epididymis and did not induce pregnancy in the partners. This was not considered related to treatment due to lack of similar findings in other males of the groups. No histopathological findings related to test substance treatment were observed in the testes, epididymides and ovaries were observed. Serum thyroxine was not altered in adult males or offspring. Offspring ano-genital distance on day 1 and visible nipple count in male pups on day 13 were not affected by treatment. An increase in the incidence of offspring with clinical signs from day of birth to day 4 was observed at 60/90 mg/kg bw/day. At 60/90 mg/kg bw/day, four litters showed no indication of milk in the stomach and all offspring from three of the litters did not survive to day 4. The remaining litter had poor offspring survival. 
Study Results: 60/90 mg/kg: Premature termination of two dams and one litter, four litters with no milk in the stomach- three died prior to day 4 and remaining litter had poor survival; no effect on ano-genital distance, visible nipple count in male offspring, no alteration of thyroxine in parental males or offspring.

Results based on critical effect: A case-control study evaluated the relationship between potential exposure to physical/chemical agents and the occurrence of intracranial tumors among employees at the Amoco Research Center (ARC) in Naperville, Illinois. Cases included employees with glioma (N=6) or benign intracranial tumors (N=6), and controls were gender- and age-matched. The employees with glioma had worked at the ARC for a median of 17 years (median 11 years for controls). The OR and 95% confidence interval for glioma was elevated and statistically significant or of borderline significance for self-reported exposure to ionized radiation (OR = 15.7 [1.4-179.4]), n-hexane (OR = infinity [1.4-infinity]), organometaliics (OR = 9.4 [1.5-59.7]) and amines other than nitrosamines (OR = 6.0 [1.0-35.7]).  The employees with benign intracranial tumors had worked at the ARC for a median of 14 years (median 6.4 years for controls). For benign intracranial tumors, the OR for self-reported exposure to ionizing radiation was statistically increased (OR = 5.4 [1.7-43.1]) and the OR for self-reported exposure to other amines was increased, but not significantly (OR = 5.2 [0.9-29.5]). Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that occupational exposures may have contributed to the excess of gliomas among C500 employees; however, results do not identify specific etiologic agents. The submission sponsor states that no firm conclusions regarding neurocarcinogenicity of particular agents can be drawn.
Study Results: Glioma: ionized radiation (OR = 15.7 [1.4-179.4]); organometaliics (OR = 9.4 [1.5-59.7]); and amines other than nitrosamines (OR = 6.0 [1.0-35.7]). Benign intracranial tumors and ionizing radiation (OR = 5.4 [1.7-43.1]) and other amines (OR = 5.2 [0.9-29.5]).

Number of Organisms per Group: Not reported

Dose/Concentrations: Vehicle control (arachis oil), 10, 100, and 1000 mg/kg-bw/day
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 90 days
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: In a 90-day oral toxicity test, Wistar rats were exposed to the test substance via oral gavage. Endpoints evaluated include hematology, blood chemistry, and histopathology. At 1000 mg/kg-bw/day, animals of both sexes showed reductions in hemoglobin, erythrocyte count, hematocrit, and mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration as well as increases in mean corpuscular volume. Males at this treatment level showed reductions in activated partial thromboplastin time, whereas females showed increases in total leucocyte count, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and platelet count. No liver histology was reported in treated groups, however, serum chemistry in males at 1000 mg/kg-bw/d showed decreases in total protein, triglycerides, cholesterol, and bilirubin and increases in albumin/globulin ratio and aspartate aminotransferase. Serum chemistry in females showed increased total protein and albumin. None of these effects were observed in animals at the 10 or 100 mg/kg-bw/day nor recovery groups. Kidney histopathology (hyaline droplets with proteinaceous casts) and splenic histopathology (increased hematopoiesis and hemosiderin) were evident in both the 100 and 1000 mg/kg-bw/day groups. After the treatment-free period, occasional instances of interstitial fibrosis and tubular dilation were present in all but one male previously treated with 1000 mg/kg-bw/day and tubular basophilia and proteinaceous casts persisted in previously affected animals. However, hyaline droplet accumulation and hematopoiesis showed complete recovery. Additionally, complete recovery in the liver and thyroid and partial recovery in the adrenals occurred in the 1000 mg/kg-bw/day group.
Study Results: 1000 mg/kg bw/day: changes in hematology and serum chemistry (males and females), kidney effects (hyaline droplets with proteinaceous casts), spleen effects (increased hematopoeisis and hemosiderin). Full recovery of hyaline droplets observed after treatment-free period; proteinaceous casts persisted in males, though were of a lesser severity. Full recovery of liver and thyroid and partial recovery of adrenals observed after treatment-free recovery period.

At 500 mg/kg/d, pathological changes were observed in the kidney including basophilic tubules, vacuolization of collecting tubules, tubule dilation in males, and vacuolization (fatty) of proximal tubular epithelium in females. Changes in the stomach at this dose included dark red patching of the mucosa in the glandular stomach with histological changes (erosion, eosinophilic globules in mucosa and eosinophil infiltration in the submucosa in males). Forestomach basal cell hyperplasia was reported in both sexes at doses greater than 3.125 mg/kg/d. Changes in the spleen (hematopoiesis of RBCs, anemia) were observed in rats treated at 500 mg/kg/d. Changes in the maxillary incisor (pale coloration, ameloblast necrosis) were observed in rats treated at 125 and 500 mg/kg/d. Study Type: Other: Range-finding study
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 28 days
Species: Mouse
Strain: Crl:CD1(ICR)
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 5/sex
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 500 (males only), 1000, 1616, and 2500 (females only) ppm
Dose Frequency: Daily (diet)
Exposure period: 28 days
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. Hematology of the 1616 ppm group revealed lower red blood cell count, lower hemoglobin levels, lower hematocrit, higher platelet counts, and higher reticulocyte counts compared to controls in both sexes. Additionally, males and females at 1616 ppm showed elevated white blood cell counts with an elevated percentage of monocytes and neutrophils. Hematology of the 1000 ppm group revealed slight increase in reticulocyte counts and higher percentages of neutrophils and monocytes in both sexes, and higher platelet counts in females. Absolute and relative weights for liver and spleen were higher than the controls for both 1616 and 1000 ppm groups. Spleen weight changes were more pronounced for males compared to females in the 1000 ppm group. Necropsy revealed roughened surface of kidneys, dark spleen with increased size in both males and females of the 1616 ppm group as well as increased spleen size in 1/5 males of the 1000 ppm group. Histopathological evaluations (evaluated only in control and 1000ppm as males 500ppm) revealed treatment-related crystals in the bile duct lumen, microgranulomas surrounding crystals in peribiliary connective tissue, subacute to chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the bile ducts, hyperplasia with hypertrophy of biliary epithelium, hypertrophy of centrilobular/midzonal hepatocytes, multifocal hepatocellular necrosis with inflammation and increased incidences of hepatocyte mitotic figures in livers of both sexes of the 1000 ppm group. In gall bladders, treatment-related hyperplasia and hypertrophy of epithelial lining and multifocal subacute to chronic inflammation were observed in both sexes of the 1000 ppm group. Treatment-related increase in extramedullary hematopoiesis were observed in the spleen of both sexes of the 1000 ppm group  
Study Results: 1616 ppm = Reduced RBC parameters, Increased reticulocyte counts, elevated platelet counts (females only), slightly elevated percentages of neutrophils and monocytes, 1000 ppm = Iincreased absolute and relative liver and spleen weights, bile duct crystals, peribiliary connective tissue microgranulomas (surrounding the crystals), bile duct inflammation, fibrosis, and hyperplasia with hypertrophy of biliary epithelium, centrilobular/midzonal hepatocytes with increased cytoplasmic eosinophilia, multifocal hepatocellular necrosis with inflammation, increased numbers of hepatocyte mitotic figures (hepatocellular proliferation), gall bladder epithelial hyperplasia and hypertrophy, extramedullary hematopoiesis in spleen with increased numbers of both erythrocytic and granulocytic precursor cells

Study Type: Oral/dermal pharmacokinetics
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Year Study Performed: 2000
Duration of Study: 29 days
Species: Rat
Strain: Sprague Dawley
Sex of Organisms: Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 15 exposed and 15 controls
Test Substance Purity: 96% (POAA was found at a level of 2.5 ng/mL in the dosing solution)
Dose/Concentrations: 5 mg/kg suspended in 2% Tween 80
Dose Frequency: Once
Exposure period: Single gavage
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The relative absorption, metabolism and elimination kinetics of PFOSA was analyzed in the rat following single oral gavage of 5 mg/kg suspended in 2% Tween 80. PFOSA was readily absorbed from the gut and was found in the liver and sera. PFOSA progressively metabolized to PFOS, which accumulated in the liver, as evidenced by high concentrations of PFOS detected in the liver, representing 22, 32 and 25% of the PFOSA dosed on days 1, 4 and 29 post dose, respectively. The half-life of elimination of PFOSA in the liver was approximately 5.2 days. There was no direct evidence of metabolism of PFOSA to PFOAA.  There were no compound related effects on body weight, liver weight, or liver/body weight ratios.
Study Results: PFOSA was readily absorbed from the gut and was found in the liver and sera. Progressive metabolism to PFOS, which accumulated in the liver. Half-life of elimination was approximately 5.2 days. No direct evidence of metabolism of PFOSA to PFOAA.

Study Type: Other: Combined repeated dose toxicity study with reproductive/developmental toxicity screening 
Protocol/guideline: Other: OECD 422
Good Lab Practices: Yes
Year Study Performed: 2017-2018
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: At least 2 months
Species: Rat
Strain: Wistar Han
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 20 (10/sex)
Test Substance Purity: 71.4% (treated as 100%) (reaction mass)
Vehicle: Distilled water
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 100, 300, and 1000 mg/kg/d
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 28 days
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were exposed to a reaction mass of CASRNs 63316-33-6 and 63316-43-8 via oral gavage. Endpoints evaluated in the parental animals include mortality, clinical signs, functional observational battery, body weight/food consumption, clinical pathology, histopathology, gross necropsy, estrous cycle (females), and T4 hormone levels (males). Salivation was observed in high dose animals, but was not considered toxicologically significant. Reduced body weight was observed in high dose males. Increased liver and kidney weights, accompanied by hepatocellular hypertrophy, were observed in both sexes at the high dose. Males also exhibited single cell necrosis in the liver; therefore, the liver effects were considered adverse in males, but not in females. Hyaline droplet accumulation was observed in the kidneys of males at the high dose, but this effect is not relevant in humans. No other observations of kidney damage were observed in both sexes; therefore, the increased kidney weight was considered to be non-adverse. Decreased bilirubin was observed in both sexes at the high dose and decreased creatinine was observed in females; however this effect did not correspond with the liver effects that were observed. No treatment-related effects were observed for all other measured parameters. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the parental NOAEL is 300 mg/kg, based on observed liver effects in males at 1000 mg/kg.
Study Results: NOAEL (parental) = 300 mg/kg

Good Lab Practices: Yes

Duration of Study: 21 hours
Species: Other: Hamster
Strain: V79 cells
Number of Organisms per Group: 1 x 10^4 cells/mL
Test Substance Purity: Active percentage in mixture 70.8% (CARN 63316-43-8), 20.9% (63316-33-6), 8.3% other
Dose/Concentration: 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, and 3500 µg/mL
Dose Frequency: Single exposure
Exposure period: 4 hours (experiment 1) and 21 hours (experiment 2)
Results based on critical effect: Precipitation was reported at doses of 2500 ug/mL without metabolic activation and 3500 ug/mL and greater with metabolic activation. Cytotoxicity was reported in experiment I at 4000 and 3500 ug/ml and higher with and without metabolic activation, respectively. Cytotoxicity was reported in experiment II at 1000 ug/ml and higher. No biologically relevant increase in polyploidy was noted in experiments I and II, with and without metabolic activation.  In experiment I without metabolic activation, an increase in chromosomal aberrations was reported at 2000 ug/mL but was not considered positive due to a lack of a dose response relationship.  In experiment I with metabolic activation, there was no increase in chromosomal aberrations. A dose-dependent increase in chromosomal aberrations was noted in experiment II at 1000 µg/mL and higher, without metabolic activation.  Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the test substance to be clastogenic in Chinese hamster V79 cells in the absence of metabolic activation.
Study Results: The test material is considered clastogenic: Positive for induction of structural chromosome aberrations in the absence of metabolic activation.

The remixed test substance heated to 315 C resulted in mean PFOA concentration of 9.6 ng/g without solvent washing and 1.4 ng/g following one ASE cycle.  The cryomilled, remixed test substance resulted in a mean PFOA concentration of 9.0 ng/g.  The cryomilled, remixed substance heated to 240 C for 24 hours resulted in a PFOA concentration of 5.0 ng/g; additional tests extending the time to 72 hours showed concentrations of 1.7 and 1.6 ng/g. Remixed test substance subjected to the thermal test for 56 hours showed the following concentrations by time period: 4h-5.4ng/g, 8h-less than 0.5ng/g, 32h-0.7ng/g, 56h-1.7ng/g, total revovery-7.8ng/g.  A standard test was run to detect other PFCAs; concentrations were 7 ng/g for PFOA, 2.1 ng/g for PFHxA, 3.8 ng/g for PFNA, 3.2 ng/g for PFDA, and < LLOQ for PFBA.  Additional testing showed: PFCAs are recovered when oxygen is present in the air stream; an increase in concentrations of each of the PFCAs were recovered when temperatures exceeded 250 C up to at least 315 C.  
Submission description: A method was developed to determine if perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) could be produced as an analyte from fluoropolymers after thermal exposure to the blended polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) powdered matrix. The test material was evaluated as is, remixed, cryomilled, or ASE solvent washed.  PFTE was heated to 315 degrees C for 24 hours in humidified (50%) air with carrier gas flow rate was 100 mL/minute, constant (std conditions). Quantification of resulting PFOA was performed as was quantification of perfluorocarboxylic acids (perfluorobutanoic (PFBA), perfluorohexanoic (PFHxA), perfluorononanoic (PFNA), and perfluorodecanoic (PFDA) acids). Results show that PFOA was recovered and quantified at level greater than the lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ). In addition, PFHxA, PFNA, PFDA were quantified, however PFBA was below the LLOQ. Alternate conditions evaluated include PFOA standard curve recovery, manipulations of remixed test substance (ASE washed, solvent washing, cryogenic milling, vacuum oven of cryomilled), single and dual reaction flask redesign, and thermal periods exceeding 24 hours.

A dose of 15,000 ppm will be used for subsequent study.

Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were administered the test substance via gavage at doses of 0, 50, 175, or 350 mg/kg/day in males and 0, 50, 175, or 500 mg/kg/day in females. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. Significant adverse effects were observed on clinical condition, body weight gain, and food intake in P generation males at 350 mg/kg/day and in females at 500 mg/kg/day. Adverse effects on reproductive capacity were also observed at these dose levels, including reduced female and male fertility, adverse effects on sperm count and morphology. Retained spermatid heads (minimal to moderate severity) were observed in males; females had depleted corpora lutea, with no effects on ovarian follicle counts and no effects on fertility. Reduced litter size at birth and impaired pup viability were observed, as well as impaired poor maternal care, and these precluded the selection of a second generation. Similar, less marked effects were observed in P generation animals at 175 mg/kg/day. No adverse effects on gestation, littering, litter size, or pup survival, growth, and development were observed in F1a or F1b litters. Effects observed in F1 generation animals included spermatid head retention (minimal/mild) in three males (vs. one control male) and irregularity of estrous cycles and differences in follicle counts; no effects on mating or fertility of F1a animals were observed. The NOAEL for parental toxicity, reproductive performance, and pre- and post-natal development was 50 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (parental toxicity, reproductive performance, and pre- and post-natal development) = 50 mg/kg/day; 175 mg/kg/day and higher = effects on clinical condition, body weight, and food intake, reduced fertility, retention of spermatids.

Results based on critical effect: Death occurred in six animals (two males, four females) in the 1000 mg/kg-bw/d group. Of these, 5 had extreme body weight loss (greater than 20%) and clinical signs of toxicity including labored respiration, gasping, and rales/squeaking, were observed in all moribund animals. Necropsy revealed distended GI tracts, and some animals exhibited pathological changes including irregular surface of forestomach and stomach foci, smaller sized organs (liver, thymus, spleen), discolored adrenal glands, and flaccid testes. Animals that survived the study exhibited  rales at all doses with dose dependent increased severity, frequency and duration. Difficulty breathing (gasping, labored breaths, deep respiration and squeaking) was observed in animals in the 1000 mg/kg-bw/d group with squeaking observed in the 300 mg/kg-bw/d group, as well. Decreased body weight and relative food consumption was observed in males in the 1000 m/kg-bw/d group. Decreased reticulocytes were observed at 1000 mg/kg-bw/and increased neutrophils were observed at 1000 mg/kg-bw/d (males only) and at greater than 300 mg/kg-bw/d (females only). All doses exhibited increased sodium levels and decreased calcium levels (females only). Decreased liver weight, decreased total protein, and increased liver enzymes (males only) were reported in 1000 mg/kg-bw/d groups and increased bile acid and ALP activity persisted throughout recovery. Decreased spleen weights were observed in males at doses greater than 300 mg/kg-bw/d.

Results based on critical effect: Reproductive organ developmental abnormalities and changes in organ weights were observed in F1 and F2 generations. An increased number of stillborn pups were observed at 3000 (F1) and 9000 ppm (F0). A decreased number of live born pups from F1 mating occurred in animals exposed to 3000 and 9000 ppm. In F2 pups treated at 9000 ppm, decreased brain, thymus, spleen, kidney, ovaries and testes weight and increased uterus weight were observed. Increased liver weight was observed in all treated groups  and increased relative kidney weights were present in pups in the 1000 and 3000 ppm groups.
Study Results: Organ weight changes in F1 at the high dose and F2 pups in all treated groups. Developmental effects present in F1 pups at 9000 ppm and F2 pups at 3000 and 9000 ppm.

Number of Organisms per Group: 4863 women

Exposure: Women employed in the synthetic rubber industry had death rates for all causes combined and all cancers that were slightly lower than the rates of generation population.  Ever-hourly employees had higher standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) for many diseases than never-hourly employees, possibly due to differences in socioeconomic status that affect health.  The study authors did not find strong, internally consistent or statistically significant associations between occupational factors and any of the cancers of strongest a priori interest (i.e., leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, other forms of lymphohematopoietic cancer (LHC), breast cancer and ovarian cancer).  The submission sponsor believes the results of the study do not provide any support for the hypothesis that employment in the synthetic rubber industry or exposure to 1,3-butadiene (BD) or the other chemicals investigated cause leukemia or other LHCs.  The absence of any association between employment factors and leukemia or other LHCs in this study may reflect the fact that the numbers of women and of person-years with relatively high exposure to BD and other chemicals were quite small.  Small increases in death from breast cancer may be due to nonoccupational determinants, many of which were not assessed.  Employees had excesses of deaths from cancers of the lung and bladder.  For these two cancers, the absence of any trend of increasing SMRs with increasing duration of employment, the lack of any exposure-response trend for cumulative exposure to BD, styrene or DMDTC and the absence of positive results of male synthetic rubber industry employees in BD monomer production or workers in industries entailing high exposure to styrene indicated that these occupational exposures may not have been responsible for the observed excesses among women in the industry.  Further, because data on tobacco use was lacking, the possibility that the excess of lung cancer was due to uncontrolled confounding by smoking could not be ruled out.
Observed Study Results: No increase in SMRs in workers exposed to BD; no evidence that employment in the synthetic rubber industry or exposure to BD causes leukemia or other LHCs.

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. Animals were administered the test substance via gavage and endpoints evaluated included mortality, clinical signs, body weight and gain, food consumption, hematology, gross necropsy, organ weight, gross necropsy and histopathology. Six females (1, 2, and 3, at low, mid, and high dose, respectively) were found dead or moribund. According to the study author, 4 out of the 6 found dead or euthanized animals were due to the test substance. Clinical signs including labored respiration, red material around nose and yellow urogenital material were observed and decreased body weights were reported in the moribund animals. No clinical signs were reported in other animals at any dose. Decreased body weight (greater than 10%), body weight gain and food consumption were observed in animals at all doses. Hematology endpoints affected included decreased reticulocyte count in males at the high dose. No liver weights were reported, however, decreased cholesterol (M, greater than or equal to 175 mg/kg/d), glucose, and bile acid (greater than or equal to 375 mg/kg/d) were observed, as well as increased triglycerides in the high dose group. Clinical chemistry indications of renal effects included increased urea nitrogen in males at 375 and 750 mg/kg/d and females at 175 and 375 mg/kg/d. Additionally, decreased thymus lymphoid cellularity was observed at 750 mg/kg/d in males and decreased weight of spleen and thyroid/parathyroid weights was reported in 375 mg/kg/d gravid females, though the study author did not consider these effects to be adverse. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the test substance LOAEL for systemic toxicity is 175 mg/kg/day based on decreased body weight gains and food consumption. The NOAEL cannot be determined, as adverse effects were observed at the lowest dose tested.
Study Results: LOAEL (systemic) = 175 mg/kg/day based on decreased body weight gains and food consumption

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. Reproductive endpoints evaluated included estrous cycles, reproductive performance, parturition, litter viability and survival, anogenital distance, and areolae/nipple anlagen. Three females were found dead and another 3 euthanized in extremis. The females found in extremis showed dystocia (175 and 315 mg/kg/d). Dose-related longer mean estrous cycles were reported at all doses. Poor fertility rates were reported at greater than or equal to 375 mg/kg/d. Exposure to doses greater than or equal to 375 mg/kg/d resulted in reduced mating and fertility, copulation in males and conception indices in females. 3/8 females had extended gestation length (23 d) at 175 mg/kg/d; extended gestation length was noted at 375 (only 4 females were gravid) but was not calculable, and no gestation was reported at 750 mg/kg/d (no gravid females). Maternal body weights were reduced at all doses. Reduced implantation sites and increased number of unaccounted for sites were observed in pregnant females at 175 and 375 mg/kg/day. Reduced number of pups born, live litter size, and postnatal survival were observed at 175 and 375 mg/kg/day. At doses greater than or equal to 375 mg/kg/d, males had reduced size and weight of coagulating gland, prostate, and seminal vesicles and decreased secretions. Histology also showed atretic follicles, reduced corpora lutea, and decreased secondary and tertiary follicles in females at all doses. Macroscopic findings included small accessory sex organs in males with corresponding microscopic findings of decreased secretion in these organs and microscopic ovarian follicle findings in females. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the test substance LOAEL for reproductive effects is 175 mg/kg/day based on longer estrous cycle and gestation lengths, low fertility, fewer implantation sites and pups born, higher numbers of unaccounted-for sites, secretion of coagulating gland, prostate and seminal vesicles in males, and reduced ovarian follicles in females. The NOAEL could not be determined as adverse findings were observed at the lowest dose tested.
Study Results: LOAEL (reproductive) = 175 mg/kg/day based on longer estrous cycles, gestation length, low fertility, fewer implantation sites, higher number of unaccounted for sites and decreased number of pups, secretion of coagulating gland, prostate and seminal vesicles in males and reduced ovarian follicles in females.

Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds that the maternal and fetal NOAEL were 1000 and 330 mg/kg/day, respectively.

Results based on critical effect: The study investigated the Influence of PFOS on lipid metabolism in rats. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. Dietary exposure of 0.02% PFOS for 7 days resulted in reduced body weight, increased liver weight, rapid and pronounced reduction in both cholesterol and triacylglycerols in serum, increased free cholesterol, and reduced cholesterol synthesis from acetate, pyruvate, and hydroxymethyl glutarate in hepatocytes. Cholesteryl ester was reduced to 50% and concentration of liver triacylglycerols was increased by about 300%. There was also some reduction in fatty acid synthesis. The activity of HMG-CoA reductase was reduced by 50% or less, and the activity of acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase was also reduced. The data suggest that the hypolipemic effect of PFOS may be mediated via a common mechanism:  impaired production of lipoprotein particles due to reduced synthesis and esterification of cholesterol together with enhanced oxidation of fatty acids in the liver.  
Study Results: 0.02%= reduced body weight, serum cholesterol, serum triacylglycerols, cholesterol synthesis from acetate, pyruvate, and hydroxymethyl glutarate in hepatocytes, fatty acid synthesis, HMG-CoA reductase and acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase activities, 50% decrease in cholesteryl ester, increased liver weight, 300% concentration increase of live triacylglycerols, and non-esterified cholesterol in the liver.

Study Results: The mixture is irritating and corrosive to rabbit eyes.

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. Maternal effects evaluated include mortality, clinical signs, maternal body weight, food intake, gross necropsy, organ weight. Developmental effects evaluated include fetal weight, sex, soft tissue and skeletal abnormalities. Maternal effects include clinical signs of piloerection at the high dose, decreased body weight and gain and food intake at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day. Developmental effects observed include visceral and skeletal malformations at doses greater than or equal to 300 mg/kg-bw/day. Visceral malformations observed include cardiac (ventricular) hypertrophy (high dose only), absent innominate artery, and aortic arch dilation. Skeletal malformations observed include moderately misshapen humerus at doses greater than or equal to 300 mg/kg-bw/day, incomplete ossification, fusion of zygomatic arch, wavy ribs, and split single thoracic centrum at the high dose. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the NOAEL for maternal toxicity is 300 mg/kg-bw/day and the NOAEL for developmental toxicity is 100 mg/kg-bw/day.
Study Results: NOAEL (maternal) = 300 mg/kg-bw/day; LOAEL (maternal) = 1000 mg/kg-bw/day; NOAEL (fetal) = 100 mg/kg-bw/day; LOAEL (fetal) = 300 mg/kg-bw/day

Study Type: Other: Combined repeated dose toxicity study with reproductive/developmental toxicity screening
Protocol/guideline: Other: OECD 422
Good Lab Practices: Yes
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: ~75 days
Species: Rat
Strain: Sprague-Dawley
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 12/sex/group (all doses; main study); 5/sex/group (control, high-dose; recovery study)
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Vehicle: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 100, 300, 1000 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 14 days premating and up to 14 days of mating in both sexes and continuing throughout gestation and until postpartum day 4 in females (main study); 14 days premating and during up to 14 days of mating (recovery study)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats (12/sex/group) were administered the test substance via gavage at 0, 100, 300, or 1000 mg/kg/day for 14 days prior to mating, up to 14 days of mating, and throughout gestation until postpartum day 4. Additional animals (5/sex/group) designated as the recovery group received the test substance for 14 days prior to mating and during up to 14 days of mating, followed by a 2-week recovery period. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. Test substance-related effects were observed only at 1000 mg/kg/day and included salivation in both sexes, reduced body weight gain in males, slightly reduced platelets in both sexes, slightly reduced eosinophils in males, increased mean serum alkaline phosphatase, total bile acids, and triglycerides in males, slightly increased prothrombin time in males, increased absolute and relative (to body and brain weight) liver weights in females, reduced absolute and relative (to body and brain weight) thymus weights in males, and microscopic changes to the liver, thymus, and testes of males. Microscopic changes observed in males included hepatic mononuclear infiltrate with or without concurrent hepatocellular single cell necrosis, lymphoid hypocellularity of the thymus, and retained spermatids in the testes. Some of the changes were reversible after 14 days of recovery, including all changes in clinical pathology and microscopic findings in all tissues except the testes. Liver weights remained slightly elevated in females (and slightly reduced in males) and retained spermatids were still observed in the testes. No effects were observed on reproductive performance or development of the F1 offspring. The NOAEL for systemic, reproductive, and developmental toxicity was 300 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: The NOAEL for systemic, reproductive, and developmental toxicity was 300 mg/kg/day; 1000 mg/kg/day = salivation in both sexes, reduced body weight gain in males, slightly reduced platelets in both sexes, slightly reduced eosinophils in males, increased mean serum alkaline phosphatase, total bile acids, and triglycerides in males, slightly increased prothrombin time in males, increased absolute and relative (to body and brain weight) liver weights in females, reduced absolute and relative (to body and brain weight) thymus weights in males, and microscopic changes to the liver, thymus, and testes of males.

Dose Frequency: ad libitum
Exposure period: GD 3-19
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The test substance was administered to pregnant rats during gestation days 3-19 in diet. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. At 7500 ppm, decreased fetal weight, reductions in the number of fetuses/litters showing incomplete ossification of the squamosal bone of the skull and no ossification of the hyoid in the skull, and an increase in the number of fetuses/litters showing showing ossification center associated with the first lumber vertebra were observed.  At 5000 ppm, a reduction in the number of fetuses/litters showing incomplete ossification of the squamosal bone of the skull and an increase in the number of fetuses/litters showing dumb-bell shaped thoracic centrum and ossification center associated with the first lumber vertebra were observed. At 2500 ppm, a reduction in the number of fetuses/litters showing no ossification of the hyoid in the skull, and an increase in the number of fetuses/litters showing ossification center associated with the first lumber vertebra were observed.
Study Results: 7500 ppm = decrease in fetal weights, reduction in fetuses/litters with incomplete ossification of the squamosal bone of the skull and no ossification of the hyoid in the skull, increase in fetuses/litters with ossification center with 1st lumbar vertebra; 5000 ppm = reduction in fetuses/litters with incomplete ossification of the squamosal bone of the skull, increase in fetuses/litters with dumb-bell thoracic centrum and ossification center with 1st lumbar vertebra;  2500 ppm = reduction in fetuses/litters with no ossification of the hyoid in the skull, increase in fetuses/litters with ossification center with 1st lumbar vertebra.

Results based on critical effect: The study is ongoing. Decreased relative liver weights in males, slightly increased absolute and relative liver weights in females, and increased absolute and relative kidney weights were reported at 2000 ppm. At 2000 ppm, very slight liver histopathologic effects were observed including  decreased cytoplasmic vacuolation (males), altered cytoplasmic homogeneity of periportal hepatocytes (females), and increased inflammatory cell aggregation with necrotic centrilobular hepatocytes. Minor kidney histopathologic effects were observed including nephron medullary outer zone cell necrosis (females), and increased basophilia of the tubules in nephrons (males) . No kidney or liver effects were noted at 600 ppm. Animals in the 2000 and 600 ppm groups had multifocal, bilaterally symmetrical degeneration and necrosis with apparent sloughing of the olfactory mucosa lining of the dorsal nasal meatus. Three males and four females of the 200 ppm group showed similar lesions at histopathology, but at a lower severity than the 600 and 2000 ppm groups. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the test substance no-effect level (NOEL) for liver and kidney effects was 600 ppm.
Study Results: NOEL (kidney and liver effects) = 600 ppm, nasal histopathological lesions were observed at all doses

Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were administered the test substance via gavage at a dose of 0 (vehicle control), 100, 300, or 1000 mg/kg for 90 days. Mortality was observed at all doses (10/30, 1/10, and 1/10 at 1000, 300, and 100 mg/kg) and necropsy revealed hepatocellular necrosis and/or degenerative renal findings. Animals at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day were not dosed from days 31 to 34, due to adverse health effects in both sexes; thereafter, the dose level was reduced to 600 mg/kg-bw/day for the remainder of the 90-day dosing period. Postmortem examinations revealed adverse effects in the liver, kidney, and urinary bladder. Macroscopic examination of animals at 300 and 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day revealed discoloration, enlargement, and accentuated lobular pattern of the liver. Histopathological changes observed in the liver of both sexes at 300 and 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day included an increased incidence and severity of hepatocellular necrosis of the centrilobular area and focal/multifocal coagulative necrosis. The postmortem liver findings correlated with increases in serum liver enzymes, total bilirubin, and bile acids, and decreases in total protein, glucose, and cholesterol at 300 and 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day. Test substance-related histopathological changes were also observed in the kidneys, including vacuolar degeneration/necrosis and granular casts in males, and a higher severity of tubular basophilia in females at 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day. Increased kidney weights and increased serum urea and creatine levels were observed in males at 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day. Dose-dependent increases in incidence and severity of hypertrophy/hyperplasia of the urothelium of the urinary bladder were observed in males and females at 300 and 1000/600 mg/kg-bw/day and was still present in recovery animals after 28 days. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the NOAEL was 100 mg/kg-bw/day.
Study Results: NOAEL = 100 mg/kg-bw/day

Study Type: Other: Repeated Inhalation Toxicity Test
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Year Study Performed: 1941
Was the Study: Measured
Species: Other: Dog
Strain: Not reported
Sex of Organisms: Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 5
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 100 ppm (target concentration); actual (measured) concentrations ranged from 30 to 140 ppm for first 30 days; during latter part of study, concentrations reached as high as 230 ppm; in addition, dogs previously exposed to 50 to 100 ppm received a single exposure above 200 ppm
Dose Frequency: 6 hours/day, 5 days/week
Exposure period: 40 to 50 exposures
Route: Inhalation
Results based on critical effect: No changes in blood pressure or circulation were noted at concentrations greater than 50 ppm.  Concentrations between 50 and 100 ppm caused a gradual increase in diastolic and pulse pressure through the 5-day exposure period during the weekdays (Mon-Fri), but recovery was generally noted over the weekend (no exposures).   Concentrations of 100 to 150 ppm caused an increase in diastolic pressure above normal levels and, although pulse pressure changes remained within normal limits, the circulation as a whole tended to become abnormal.  Animals not previously exposed to the test substance could withstand one or two 6-hour exposures at concentrations above 200 ppm without any serious abnormality; however, dogs previously exposed to 50 to 100 ppm were especially prone to circulatory collapse when subsequently exposed to concentrations above 200 ppm.  In one case, a single exposure above 200 ppm caused mortality in an animal previously exposed to 50 to 100 ppm.  Necropsy of this animal revealed dilatation of all blood vessels throughout the body and signs of circulatory failure and collapse.  At concentrations higher than 100 ppm, electrocardiograms indicated acute anoxia of the heart muscle, as indicated by a low voltage T wave or even isoelectric or dibasic T wave.
Study Results: No NOAEL/LOAEL; circulatory effects at concentrations of 100 ppm and higher

Study Type: Other: Two generation reproduction/development toxicity test
Protocol/guideline: Other: OPPTS 870.3800 (OECD 416) - Reproduction and Fertility Effects
Year Study Performed: 2002
Duration of Study: 2 generations
Species: Rat
Strain: Sprague-Dawley
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 30/sex/group
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Vehicle: Corn oil
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 10, 100, and 1000 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Daily: 7 days/week (gavage)
Exposure period: Parental: at least 10 weeks prior to mating through mating; F1 parental animals: PND 22 through mating 
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Clinical signs of toxicity, body weights and food consumption, gross necropsy and macroscopic examination were recorded for the P and F1 parental animals. Histopathological examinations were conducted on reproductive tissue of P and F1 animals in the control and 1000 mg/kg/day dose groups and in animals in the remaining treatment groups that did not mate, conceive, or sire. Organ weights (brain, spleen, and thymus) and gross lesions were recorded for F1 pups and F2 pups (1/sex/litter). The substance had no effect on survival of rats in parental, F1, or F2 generations. Low incidence of mortality was considered to be incidental and unrelated to treatment. In F1 males, the only effect of treatment was a reduction in body weight and body weight gain at 1000 mg/kg/day. There was no effect in either parental generation in clinical examinations, body weights or food consumption, or organ weights. In addition, there was no effect in the F1 or F2 pups on body weights, clinical findings, sex ratios, macroscopic findings or organ weights. At 100 and 1000 mg/kg/day, there were some treatment-related effects on thyroid parameters (T3 and T4); however, TSH levels were unaffected. The only treatment-related neurotoxic effect was a reduction in the thickness of the parietal cortex of the Day 11 F2 pups at 1000 mg/kg/day. This change was not accompanied by any histologic changes. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOEL for parental toxicity is 100 mg/kg/day based on reduced body weight and body weight gain in males at 1000 mg/kg/day; the NOEL for thyroid effects is 10 mg/kg/day (based on reduced T3 and T4 levels at the 100 and 1000 mg/kg/day dose levels).
Study Results: NOEL: 10 mg/kg/day LOEL: 100 mg/kg/day  (based on reduced T3 and T4 levels at the 100 and 1000 mg/kg/day dose levels).

Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. In a prenatal developmental screening test, female rats were exposed to the test substance on gestational day 6 to 19. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. The high-dose group was sacrificed on GD 16 due to maternal toxicity (piloerection, decreased food consumption and body weight loss or decreased body weight change). The submitter found found that 250 mg/kg bw/day exceeded the maximum tolerated dose. The 100 mg/kg bw/day group showed decreased body weights, corrected body weight gain, kidney and spleen weights, placental weights, reduced fetal weights, and increased liver weights. Additionally, the test found that 8 out of 10 litters of the 100 mg/kg bw/day group had an increased number of soft tissue variations. Skeletal variations were also observed in 8 out of 10 litters with 19 pups; dumbbell ossification of the thoracid centrum was found in 8 out of 10 litters with 16 pups; incomplete ossification of supraoccipital in 10 out of 10 litters with 25 pups. In the 100 mg/kg bw/day group, the liver weights were relatively higher (10%) than control.   
Study Results: 250 mg/kg bw/day = decreased body weight, decreased food consumption, piloerection; 100 mg/kg bw/day = decreased body weights, decreased corrected body weight gain, decreased placental weights, reduced fetal weights, increased soft tissue and skeletal variations

Study Type: Other: Developmental Toxicity Study
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported

Was the Study: Measured

Species: Rat
Strain: Fischer 344
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 25 timed-pregnant rats
Test Substance Purity: 99.4%
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 100, 250, or 500 mg/kg/day in corn oil
Dose Frequency: Daily gavage
Exposure period: GD 6-15
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The test substance induced maternal toxicity following exposure to 500 mg/kg/day on GD 6-15. Maternal toxicity consisted of clinical signs (hypoactivity, ataxia, audible respiration, ocular discharge, and periocular encrustation) and increased absolute and relative liver weight. There were no treatment-related maternal deaths. Developmental toxicity was observed at 250 mg/kg/day, as evidenced by reduced skeletal ossification.  In addition, one visceral variation (dilated lateral ventricles on the brain with no tissue variation) was observed at 500 mg/kg. No embryotoxicity or teratogenicty were apparent. The NOAELs for maternal and developmental toxicity were 250 and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively.
Study Results: NOAEL (maternal): 250 mg/kg/day. NOAEL (developmental): 100 mg/kg/day. No treatment-related maternal deaths. Maternal toxicity at 500 mg/kg/day: hypoactivity, ataxia, audible respiration, ocular discharge, periocular encrustation, increased absolute/relative liver weight. No embryotoxicity or teratogenicity. One visceral variation (dilated lateral ventricles on the brain with no tissue variation) at 500 mg/kg/day. Increased number of fetal skeletal variations (delayed ossification) at 250 and 500 mg/kg/day.

Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were administered the test substance via gavage once daily at 0, 100, 300, or 1000 mg/kg-bw/day for 90 days. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. At the end of the dosing period, body weight gain was decreased by 10% in males at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day, relative to controls. Serum urea was significantly increased in females at 300 and 1000 mg/kg-bw/day. Slight increases in liver weight were observed in males at 300 mg/kg-bw/day and higher and in females at all doses, and slight increases in kidney weight were observed in males at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day, relative to controls; however, the increases were not statistically significant. Test substance-related pale kidneys were observed in both sexes at all doses, and were accompanied by minor severity tubular swelling/vacuolation in both sexes at all doses. In males, the incidence and severity of hyaline inclusions in tubular cells was strongly increased; this was not due to increasing alpha2u-globulin and was instead considered to be due to increasing lysosome activity storing either the test substance or a metabolite. Tubular cell necrosis and the formation of granular casts was also observed in males at all dose levels. An increased incidence of minimal tubular basophilia was observed at 100 and 300 mg/kg-bw/day, but not at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day, which was suggestive of regeneration at 100 and 300 mg/kg-bw/day, but limited regenerative ability at 1000 mg/kg-bw/day. Mottled and pale livers in males at 300 mg/kg-bw/day and higher and in females at all dose levels was associated with an increased incidence of minimal severity hepatocellular hypertrophy and vacuolation, both of which showed a dose-related increase in incidence and severity. 
Study Results: 1000 mg/kg-bw/day = decreased body weight gain in males; 300, 1000 mg/kg-bw/day = increased serum urea in females and histopathological changes in the liver of males; 100, 300, 1000 mg/kg-bw/day = histopathological changes in the kidneys of both sexes.

Good Lab Practices: Yes

Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: Approx 2 days
Species: Mouse
Strain: L5178Y cell line
Number of Organisms per Group: 10E7 cells

Dose/Concentration: 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 7.5 mM (without activation); 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 7.0, 8.0, 8.5, 9 mM (with activation)
Dose Frequency: Single exposure
Exposure period: 4 hours
Results based on critical effect: Please note the document is a sanitized version of the 8e submission. L5178Y mouse lymphoma cells were exposed to the test substance at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, and 7.5 mM without S9 metabolic activation and 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 7.0, 8.0, 8.5, and 9 mM with S9 metabolic activation for 4 hours in DMSO. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. A biologically relevant, statistically significant increase in the mutant frequency was found with S9; no such increase was found without S9. The negative and positive controls gave the expected responses. The test substance was found to be clastogenic, based on an increased number of small colonies at mutagenic concentrations. Growth inhibition was observed with and without S9, based on relative total growth (RTG); at the highest concentrations evaluated without (7.5 mM) and with S9 (9 mM), RTG values were 14.5% and 13.9%, respectively. The test substance was mutagenic in the presence of S9. Negative and positive controls gave the expected responses.
Study Results: Positive for mutagenicity with S9; negative without S9.

Study Type: Other: 13-week dermal toxicity study in rats with spermatogenic assessment
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 13 weeks
Species: Rat
Strain:  Not reported
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 12/sex (main study, assessment of subchronic toxicity after 13 weeks/65 applications); 5 males (additional study group, assessment of spermatogenic endpoints after 37 applications)
Test Substance Purity:  Not reported
Vehicle: 0.9% saline
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 100, 300, and 1000 mg/kg/day
Dose Frequency: 5 days/week for 13 weeks/65 applications (main study) or for 37 applications (additional study group)
Exposure period: 6 hours/day (occluded)
Route: Dermal
Results based on critical effect: No mortalities or clinical signs of toxicity were noted for any group.  Limited evidence of dermal irritation occurred (doses not specified).  Mean food consumption was not affected in animals administered the test substance; however, mean body weights and body weight gains were reduced in males and females at 1000 mg/kg/day after 13 weeks of exposure.  Hematology and serum chemistry parameters were not changed, relative to controls, and no test substance-related gross or microscopic lesions were observed at necropsy.  Male rats exhibited a decrease in the mean number of sperm in the testis and mean sperm production rate at 300 and 1000 mg/kg/day.  In addition, there was a decrease in the mean percentage of motile sperm at 1000 mg/kg/day.  The 13-week dermal NOEL was 100 mg/kg/day in male rats and 300 mg/kg/day in female rats.
Study Results: 13-week rat dermal NOEL = 100 mg/kg/day (males) and 300 mg/kg/day (females).

Results based on critical effect: In a 14-day repeated dose range-finding study, male and female rats were administered the test substance daily via gavage. Endpoints evaluated include mortality, body weight changes, clinical signs, clinical chemistry, hematology, gross pathology, and organ weight. In the low dose group, no mortalities or other treatment-related adverse findings were noted. In the high dose group, one female was found dead on study day 14. No information on other evaluated endpoints was provided.
Study Results: 1000 mg/kg bw/day: 1 female dead on day 14, poor condition in 2 males, respiration sounds in 2 males and 1 female, labored respiration in 1 male, and body weight loss in males and females in the first 3 days.

Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following results. Two females at 90 mg/kg bw/day were euthanized around the time of parturition and the dose was lowered to 60 mg/kg bw/day. Study Results: 60/90 mg/kg bw/day= mortality, clinical signs, reduced prostate weight in parental males, total litter loss, reduced offspring body weight; 30 mg/kg bw/day= total litter loss; 15 mg/kg bw/day= no effects of treatment.

Results based on critical effect: Males and females exhibited dose-dependent reductions in body weight gain at doses of 5 mg/kg/day and higher, relative to controls.  Gestational maternal body weight gain was reduced at 15 mg/kg/day, relative to controls.  There were no test substance-related effects on the number of pregnancies.  In females (10/group) sacrificed on gestation day 10 for intrauterine examination, no increase in resorptions was observed, but the number of implantations was reduced at 15 mg/kg/day (mean of 11.1, compared to 15.6 in controls).  At parturition, a reduction in the mean number of pups delivered occurred at 10 mg/kg/day (12.8 pups) and 15 mg/kg/day (10.3 pups), compared to controls (15.6 pups).  Other perinatal effects observed at greater than/equal to 10 mg/kg/day included an increase in the percentage of stillborn pups (4.8% at 10 mg/kg/day and 32.4% at 15 mg/kg/day, compared to 1.4% in controls) and a reduction in pup survival during days 1-4 of lactation (30.2% survival at 10 mg/kg/day and 1.2% survival at 15 mg/kg/day).  Most pup deaths at the high-dose level occurred within 24 hours after birth.  No parental effects were reported at 1 mg/kg/day and no perinatal effects were reported at 5 mg/kg/day.
Study Results: No NOAEL/LOAEL values were reported. Parental toxicity was evident (reduced body weight gain) in males and females during premating at greater than/equal to 5 mg/kg/day and in females during gestation at 15 mg/kg/day. Reduced implantations at 15 mg/kg/day, reduced mean number of pups delivered, increased percentage of stillborn pups, and reduced pup survival at greater than/equal to 10 mg/kg/day.

Study Type: Other: Combined repeated dose toxicity study with reproductive/developmental toxicity screening
Protocol/guideline: Other: OECD 422
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: At least 70 days
Species: Rat
Strain: Wistar
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 10/sex (treated groups); 6/sex (recovery groups)
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Vehicle: Paraffin oil
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 50, 100, and 150 (reduced to 125) mg/kg-bw/day
Dose Frequency: Daily (gavage)
Exposure period: 28 days (pre mating and mating) (males); up to 54 days (pre-mating, mating, during gestation, and up to PND 3) (females)
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: Wistar rats (10/sex/dose) were treated with 0, 50, 100, or 150 mg/kg/day of the test substance (formulated in paraffin oil) in a combined repeated dose oral toxicity study with the reproduction/developmental toxicity screening test. The 150 mg/kg/day dose was reduced to 125 mg/kg/day after the pre-mating period due to observed mortality and morbidity. Mortality and morbidity occurred in a dose-dependent manner with 4 males in the mid dose group, 5 males and 5 females in the high dose group and 4 males and 3 females in the high dose recovery group. Clinical signs of toxicity included  progressive ataxia, paresis (mainly hindlimbs) and hypotonia in the mid and high dose groups. Abnormal breathing was observed in moribund animals; additional signs of toxicity included decreased spontaneous activity, wasp waist, and piloerection at doses of 100 mg/kg/day and higher. Adverse changes in several parameters of the functional observation battery (number of rearings, ataxic and hypotonic gait,  reduced equilibrium reflex, positional passivity, visual placing, grip strength, sensitivity to pinching the tail, limb tone, hind limb reflex, toe pinch reflex, righting on the ground, and air righting reflex) were reported; these effects were generally still present following the recovery period. Adverse changes in body weight, body weight development, and food consumption were observed at doses of 100 mg/kg/day and higher. Treatment-related changes in histopathology included progressive polyneuropathy in peripheral nerves at doses of 100 mg/kg/day and higher; these effects remained present following the recovery period. Lung disease with an increase of subacute peri/vasculitis was reported at 150 mg/kg/day.  Hepatocellular hypertrophy/necrosis was observed in several animals at doses of 100 mg/kg/day and higher (significance not specified); this effect was not present following the recovery period. Myofiber atrophy and/or degeneration of minor severity.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the NOAEL for systemic toxicity is 50 mg/kg/day and the LOAEL is 100 mg/kg/day based on increased incidence of mortality, clinical signs of toxicity, changes in body weight and body weight gain, and changes in histopathology (polyneuropathy in peripheral nerves)
Study Results: NOAEL = 50 mg/kg/day; LOAEL = 100 mg/kg/day

Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentration: 0, 0.09, 0.1, 0.26 and 0.47 mg/L (measured)
Route: Inhalation
Exposure period: 4 hours
Results based on critical effect: In an acute inhalation toxicity test, rats were exposed to the test substance nose-only at measured concentrations of 0, 0.09, 0.1, 0.26 and 0.47 mg/L for 4 hours. The mortality incidence was 10/10 animals at 0.47 mg/L and 9/10 animals at 0.26 mg/L. At 0.47 mg/kg, the following was observed: abnormal breathing, uncoordinated movement, tremors, lying on the side, dark red and tan mottling of the lungs, fluid in the trachea, stomach dilation and gas. At 0.26 mg/L. abnormal breathing, increased respiratory rate, tremors, hunched posture, cool to touch, decreased activity, reddened skin around nares, lying on side, dark red and red mottling of the lungs, failure of the lungs to collapse, fluid in the trachea, and red/tan discoloration of the thymus. Clinical signs of toxicity at 0.1 mg/L included abnormal breathing, swelling of muzzle, and liquid discharge from the muzzle. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the LC50 is 0.17 mg/L for males, 0.14 mg/L for females, and 0.15 mg/L for both combined.
Study Results: LC50 = 0.17 mg/L (males); 0.14 mg/L (females), 0.15 mg/L (combined sexes)

There were no motile sperm in 4/10 males at the high dose. Progressive motility at all dose levels was also lower than controls in a dose-related manner. Study Results: Ongoing study. Reduction in sperm concentration and motility at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day.  Increase in the number of abnormal sperms and enlarged kidneys  in males at 300 mg/kg/day.

Study Type: Inhalation developmental toxicity study
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: Approximately 16 days (exposure on GD 7-16 with sacrifice on GD 22)
Species: Rat
Strain: Crl:CD BR
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 25
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 5000, 20,000, and 50,000 ppm
Dose Frequency: Daily
Exposure period: Gestation days (GD) 7-16
Route: Inhalation
Results based on critical effect: No maternal deaths were reported following inhalation exposure at doses up to 50,000 ppm.  Diminished alerting responses were observed throughout the exposure period (GD 7-16) at 20,000 and 50,000 ppm.  Other evidence of maternal toxicity was seen at 50,000 ppm and included reduced maternal body weight gain and reduced maternal food consumption.  No evidence of maternal toxicity was observed at 5000 ppm.  An increased incidence of retarded sternebral ossification was observed in rat pups from mothers exposed to 20,000 and 50,000 ppm. The incidence of this finding was not dose-related (finding was more prevalent at 20,000 ppm).  The incidences were 8(5), 10(5), 17(10), and 14(10) fetuses(litters) for the 0, 5000, 20,000, and 50,000 ppm groups, respectively.  The increased incidence of retarded ossification was not considered to be test substance-related and was instead considered to be the result of a low control group value (8 fetuses from 5 litters) given available historical control data from the laboratory.
Study Results: No NOAEL/LOAEL determined; maternal toxicity (reduced body weight gain/food consumption) at 50,000 ppm; maternal clinical signs (diminished alerting responses) at greater than/equal to 20,000 ppm; no test substance-related developmental effects.

Study Type: Preliminary developmental toxicity screen
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Year Study Performed: 1998
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 15 days (exposure on GD 6-19 with sacrifice on GD 20)
Species: Rat
Strain: Crl:CD BR VAF/Plus (Sprague-Dawley)
Sex of Organisms: Female
Number of Organisms per Group: 8 pregnant rats/group
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 32.5, 100, 325, and 650 mg/kg/day (dosage volume of 5 mL/kg)
Dose Frequency: Once daily, gavage
Exposure period: GD 6-19
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: In a preliminary dose range-finding study conducted for a definitive developmental toxicity study, the test substance was lethal to 1/8 and 4/8 dams after exposure to 325 and 650 mg/kg, respectively on GD 6-19. Clinical signs in animals that died included weight loss, red perioral substance, excess salivation, urine-stained abdominal fur, ptosis, soft/liquid feces, and loss of righting reflexes. Necropsy of these animals revealed red frothy material in the lungs and trachea, and red cardiac mucosa of the stomach. In one rat that was sacrificed early in moribund condition, necropsy revealed numerous red areas on the nonglandular surface of the stomach. There was a 100% resorption of conceptuses in two litters at 650 mg/kg and increased early resorptions with reduced litter size at 325 mg/kg. Fetal body weights were reduced at 325 mg/kg. These effects were associated with maternal toxicity. Based on the results of this study, doses of 0, 25, 100, and 200 mg/kg are recommended for the definitive developmental study.  The no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) is expected to be 25 mg/kg for both maternal and embryo-fetal toxicity, and the lowest observed adverse effect level (LOAEL) is expected to be 200 mg/kg.
Study Results: From this preliminary dose range-finding study, the full developmental study dosages were determined as 0, 25, 100, 200 mg/kg/day. Expected NOAEL: 25 mg/kg/day (for maternal and embryo-fetal toxicity) and expected LOAEL: 200 mg/kg/day.

Exposure occurred 6 hours/day for 5 consecutive days and animals were observed for 3 weeks after exposure. Effects revealed after brochoalveolar lavage of animals in the 1000 mg/m3 dose group included increases in total cell and absolute and relative neutrophil cell counts, total protein,  gamma-glutyamyl transferase activity, alkaline phosphatase activity, and lactate dehydrogenase activity, and increases in monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 and osteopontin levels. Histopathological effects the lungs of animals at 300 and 1000 mg/m3 included alveolar histiocytosis and epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia of the terminal briochioles and alveolar ducts, inflammation (mixed-cellular) of the lungs was also observed at 1000 mg/m3. No treatment-related adverse findings were observed at the end of the 3-week recovery period in animals of the 1000 mg/m3 group. There were no treatment-related effects in animals exposed to 100 mg/m3.  
Study Results: 1000 mg/m3 = increased total cell and neutrophil counts, increased protein levels and gamma-glutamyl transferase, alkaline phosphatase, and lactate dehydrogenase activities, alveolar histiocytosis, epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia, and increased inflammation. 300 mg/m3 = increased gamma-glutamyl transferase and alkaline phosphatase, alveolar histiocytosis, and epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia. On Lactation Day 1, reduced body weight (greater than or equal to a 5% change from controls) was reported in F1 pups born to dams in the 1.5 mg/kg/day group and in male F1 pups born to dams in the 0.6 mg/kg/day group. F1 pups (male and female) born to dams in the 1.5 mg/kg/day group had significantly reduced body weight on post-natal days (PND) 24, 27, 32, 39, and 42. There were no significant effects on the pregnancy outcomes of treated dams (number of implantation sites, litter size, number of live litter size, or sex ratio). There were no significant effects on developmental outcomes in F1 pups regarding overall development, ano-genital distance (AGD), onset of preputial separation or vaginal opening, weight and tissue morphology of reproductive organs, or thyroid morphology. 
Study Results: 0.6 mg/kg/day: Reduced body weight (≥5% change) on lactation day 1 in F1 pups (male)  1.5 mg/kg/day: Reduced body weight (≥5% change) (lactation day 1), reduced body weight on PNDs 24, 27, 32, 39, 42 in F1 pups.

Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported

Species: Mouse
Strain: CD-1
Sex of Organisms: Female

Test Substance Purity: 99.9%
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 0.5, 5.0, or 10.0 mL/kg/day
Dose Frequency: Daily, gavage
Exposure period: GD 6-15
Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: The test substance produced maternal and fetotoxicity/developmental delay following oral exposure on GD 6-15. Maternal effects included clinical signs of toxicity (hypoactivity, audible and rapid respiration) and reduced relative kidney weights at 10.0 mL/kg. Gravid uterine weight was also slightly reduced at 5.0 and 10.0 mL/kg.  There were no treatment-related maternal deaths and no abortions.  Fetotoxicity was evidenced by reduced fetal body weights and reduced ossification in several skeletal districts at 10.0 mL/kg and in the head region at 5.0 mL/kg. There was no significant embryotoxicity or teratogenicity at any dose level. The NOEL for maternal and fetal toxicity was 5.0 mL/kg/day.
Study Results: NOEL (maternal): 5.0 mL/kg/day (clinical signs, increased relative kidney wt at 10.0 mL/kg/day). NOEL (developmental): 0.5 mL/g/day (reduced fetal body wt and skeletal variations at 5.0 and 10.0 mL/kg/day). No treatment-related maternal deaths.No significant embryotoxicity or teratogenicity.

Study Type: Onconogenicity
Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported
Good Lab Practices: Yes
Year Study Performed: 1981
Was the Study: Measured
Duration of Study: 2 years
Species: Rat
Strain: Fischer 344
Sex of Organisms: Female; Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 120/sex
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 10, 33, or 100 ppm
Frequency of Doses: 6 hours per day, 5 days per week
Survival Rate: 94 surviving animals (24 rats died during exposure weeks 64 and 65)
Exposure period: 2 years
Route: Inhalation
Results based on critical effect: The test substance produced oncogenicity in rats after exposure via inhalation for 2 years. Effects included an increased incidence of mononuclear cell leukemia (dose-dependent in females), an increased incidence in the number of malignant neoplasms in females, and an increased incidence of peritoneal mesothelioma in males at 33 and 100 ppm. The incidence of pituitary adenoma was not significantly increased in comparison to controls; however, the onset was accelerated at 100 ppm. Additional effects included depressed body weight gain and increased mortality at 33 and 100 ppm, a slight depression in erythrocyte count and hemoglobin values in females at 100 ppm after 12 months, and skeletal muscle atrophy in animals from the 100 ppm group at the final sacrifice.  Gross and microscopic examination of animals that died revealed no pathological findings severe enough to explain the cause of death.
Study Results: Increased incidence of mononuclear cell leukemia (dose-related in females). Increased number of malignant neoplams in females at 33 and 100 ppm. Increased incidence of peritoneal mesothelioma in males at 33 and 100 ppm.  Depressed body weight gain and increased mortality at 33 and 100 ppm. Slight depression in erythrocyte count and hemoglobin value in females at 100 ppm after 12 months. Skeletal muscle atrophy at 100 ppm.

Protocol/guideline: Other: Not reported

Species: Rat

Sex of Organisms: Female; Male

Dose Frequency: Daily

Results based on critical effect: Male and female rats were administered the test substance via gavage at 0, 100, 300, or 1000 mg/kg/day in corn oil. Based on the results, the submission sponsor finds the following. Mean absolute and relative liver weights were increased at 1000 mg/kg/day in parental males and females. Treatment-related necrosis, with or without inflammation, of individual hepatocytes, was observed at 300 and 1000 mg/kg/day in parental males and at 100 mg/kg/day in females. The necrosis of individual hepatocytes was considered to be adverse.
Study Results: 1000 mg/kg-bw/day = increased liver weights in males and females; necrosis, with or without inflammation, of individual hepatocytes in males and females, and also in males at 300 mg/kg-bw/day.

The following test item-related clinical observations were recorded: slight to marked corneal opacity (grade 1-3), moderate iritis (grade 1), slight to obvious conjunctival redness (grade 1-2), slight to marked conjunctival chemosis (grade 1-3), and slight to severe discharge (grade 1-3).  Additionally, contracted pupil, desquamation of corneal epithelium, corneal lesions (grade 1 - 4), marginal vascularization of the cornea in a circumscribed area as well as vascularization into the central part of the cornea in a circumscribed area were seen in the animal within 96 hours or 21 days. Due to the strong swelling of the conjunctiva at hour 1 no evaluation of the scleral vessels was possible in both animals. Neither reading nor assessment of reaction to the fluorescein instillation due to the strong swelling of the conjunctiva was possible in one of the animals at hour 24. Thereafter, injected scleral vessels in a circumscribed or circular area could be noted in the animals until hour 96 or day 28. One animal showed an impaired general state from study day 1 until day 2, the other animal showed an impaired general state at day 0 and 1, possibly caused by the repeated injections of the analgesics until habituation. The ocular reactions were reversible in the first tested animal within 7 days. The ocular reactions were not reversible in the second tested animal within 28 days after application. Slight corneal opacity (grade 1) and injected scleral vessels in a circumscribed area were still observed in this animal at study termination on day 29. Mean scores calculated for each animal over 24, 48 and 72 hours were 2.0 and 2.3 for corneal opacity, 1.0 and 0.3 for iris lesions as well as 2.0 and 2.0 for redness of the conjunctiva and for chemosis.  Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the test substance causes serious damage to rabbit eyes.

Observed Study Results: The submission refers to the test article as "crude oil". Application of 1-2 cm of oil on test plots in 1972 continued to impair reseeding efforts a year later. Growth on oiled plots was much less than on unoiled plots. Practically no growth occurred on plots treated with 2 cm and it was concluded that this amount was a "heavy application".  Transplanting was more successful than reseeding, with partial growth occurring 1 year later. Survival of transplanted plugs varied from 50 to 100% by the end of the first growing season.  Although fertilization and tillage aided in oil mitigation, overall yields on treated plots were 1/4 - 1/5 of those on unoiled plots.  It appeared that nitrogen content of soil was inversely related to oil quantity.  A 3/4 cm rate of oil application appeared to exert adequate effects while still permitting growth to differentiate between species tolerance to oil toxicity. It was also determined that burning as a method of oil removal was much more detrimental to plant growth in the summer as opposed to the winter.

Route: Oral
Results based on critical effect: In a prenatal toxicity study the test material containing 0.04 ppm formaldehyde was administered to pregnant rats daily by gavage. Transient reduction in maternal body weights (GD 6-8) were observed but were not statistically significant. No other maternal toxicity was observed at any dose. At 900 mg/kg/day, developmental effects included two litters with malformed fetuses (absent and fused ribs, hemivertebrae, sternoschisis, gastroschisis, macropthalmia, and absent stomach and intestines), increased incidence in fetal variations (bipartite ossification of the thoracic and/or lumbar centrum, misaligned sternebrae, and supernumerary ribs), and reduced mean fetal weights (10% lower than the control group). No evidence of developmental toxicity was observed at 300 mg/kg/day and lower. Based on these results, the submission sponsor finds that the developmental NOAEL is 300 mg/kg/day, and LOAEL is 900 mg/kg/day; NOAEL for maternal toxicity was 900 mg/kg/day, highest tested dose.
Study Results: Developmental NOAEL = 300 mg/kg/day, and LOAEL = 900 mg/kg/day based on malformations and reduced fetal weight; maternal NOAEL = 900 mg/kg/day, highest tested dose

Species: Rat
Strain: Wistar
Sex of Organisms: Male
Number of Organisms per Group: 5
Test Substance Purity: Not reported
Dose/Concentrations: 0, 0.2, 0.5, and 10 mg/m3
Dose Frequency: Daily
Exposure period: 6 hours/day
Route: Inhalation
Results based on critical effect: In a range-finding study for a 90-day inhalation study, groups of male rats were exposed to the test substance for six hours daily for five consecutive days. The following effects were noted at 10 mg/m3: accelerated respiratory rate (days 4 and 5), reduced body weight gain, increased hemoglobin and hematocrit, increased absolute and relative neutrophil and relative monocyte counts, and decreased relative monocyte count. Lung effects noted at 2 and 10 mg/m3 included mixed-cellular inflammation (minimal at 2 mg/m3 and slight to severe at 10 mg/m3; alveolar, peribronchial, peribronchiolar, and perivascular), and epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia in bronchi and bronchioles, including terminal bronchioles (minimal and in 2/5 animals at 2 mg/mg3, slight to moderate and in all animals at 10 mg/m3). Lung effects at 10 mg/m3 only included statistically significantly increased mean absolute and relative weights, slight to severe type-II pneumocyte hyperplasia in all animals (with atypia in 1/5 animals), and minimal to moderate alveolar edema in 2/5 animals. Effects in the trachea at 10 mg/m3 included minimal to slight epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia in 4/5 animals. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) results showed the following effects at 2 and 10 mg/m3: increased total cell and absolute and relative neutrophil counts, decreased relative macrophage counts, and increased total protein levels, lactate dehydrogenase, beta-N-acetyle gluocosaminidase, and glutamyl transferase activities. BAL effects observed only at 10 mg/m3 included increased total cell and absolute and relative monocyte and eosinophil counts, increased absolute lymphocyte and epithelial cell counts, and increased alkaline phosphatase activity. No adverse effects were noted at 0.5 and 0.2 mg/m3. The recovery group exposed to 10 mg/m3 showed accelerated respiration from day 4 to 12, reduced body weight gain during the exposure period, increased total cell and absolute and relative neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte counts in BAL, increased absolute but decreased relative counts in BAL, increased total protein levels, lactate dehydrogenase, alkaline phosphatase, beta-acetyl glucosaminidase, and gamma-glutamyl transferase activities in BAL. Lung effects noted in the recovery group included statistically significantly elevated absolute and relative weights, minimal to slight mixed-cellular inflammation in 3/5 animals (alveolar, peribronchial, peribronchiolar, and perivascular), and alveolar histiocytosis in all animals (slight to moderate) accompanied by cell debris.
Study Results: Effects on bronchoalveolar lavage results (increased total cell and absolute and relative neutrophil counts, decreased relative macrophage counts, increased total protein levels, lactate dehydrogeanase, beta-N-acetyle glucosaminidase, and gamma-glutamyl transferase activities) and effects in lungs (mixed-cellular inflammation in alveolar, peribronchial, peribronchiolar, and perivascular tissue and epithelial hypertrophy/hyperplasia in bronchi and bronchioles) were noted at 2 mg/m3, 10 mg/m3, and in the recovery group.
